## Gates — orchestrator-run, per commit

Per the plan's corrected figures. All 29 files stay on disk throughout; each commit selects contents
**by path**. All timings measured on this machine.

| | Command | Time | COMMIT 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 15s | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| G2 | `npx vitest run` | 15s | 354/22 | 354/22 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 |
| G3 | `npm run lint` | 15s | 17 err / **15 warn** | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 |
| G4 | Storybook interaction + a11y | ~2 min | 100/22 | 100/22 | 102/23 | 102/23 | 105/24 |
| G5 | `npm run audit:tokens` | 0.4s | 19→**14** | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| G6 | Developer, live PDP | — | **stop** | — | — | **stop** | — |

**G3 is the load-bearing one at COMMIT 1** — the only signal that can catch a missed Step 1 removal.
Baseline 15, ceiling 25 if all 10 dead imports are left. Error count is a 17 invariant throughout.

**Inner loop (~45s, offline, zero repo writes)** — G1 → scoped G2 → full G2 → G3 → G5. A scoped
Vitest run is **8× faster** and is the right thing during rework: `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-detail`
is 1.8s against 15s for the full suite. Full G2 before the commit, always.

**G4 does not need `http-server`, and does not need `build-storybook`.** The CI recipe uses
`npx http-server storybook-static` (and `http-server` is genuinely absent from `package.json`,
`node_modules`, and global). But `test-storybook`'s default `--url` is already
`http://127.0.0.1:6006`, which is exactly what `npm run storybook` (`storybook dev -p 6006`) serves:

```
npm run storybook &                                    # dev server, port 6006
npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 120000
node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci
```

No static build, nothing written to `storybook-static/`, and incremental webpack rebuilds between
iterations instead of a ~2-4 min cold build each time. `test-storybook` and `wait-on` both exist in
`node_modules/.bin`. Two caveats: it is a long-lived background process the loop must own and reap,
and **Playwright's chromium binary is a prerequisite** — check `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/`
before the first run, because installing it needs network. Zero-dependency fallback if dev mode
misbehaves: `python3 -m http.server 6006 --directory storybook-static` against an existing build.

**G4 is more aggressive than it looks.** `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `a11y: { test: 'error' }`,
so **all 100 stories are a11y assertions**, not just the 37 carrying a `play`. A purely-visual new
story can fail this gate.

**Playwright is out of the loop entirely.** No PDP spec exists — `e2e/tests/` holds exactly one file
(two homepage smoke tests). `ProductPage.js` scaffolding exists but nothing uses it, there is no
`e2e_pdp` allow-list group, and change-scoping for our diff falls back to the full suite, which is
those same two homepage tests. Writing one is blocked by a hard human gate anyway: the Gherkin-first
workflow requires Lead QA sign-off *before* any Playwright code. Not a gap this loop can close.

**Two gates the loop is the only enforcement for.** Neither `tsc --noEmit` nor `audit:tokens` is
wired into any CI workflow — `qa.yml` has no typecheck job at all. So G1 and G5 are not "extra
diligence", they are the only place those checks happen before merge.

## Loop hazards — hard-code these as guardrails

Three ways an automated loop silently corrupts its own signal here:

1. **`npm run lint` can be turned into a writer.** `package.json` defines
   `"lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix"`, and `pwa-kit-dev lint` forwards `--`-args verbatim into a
   shell `execSync`. Plain `npm run lint` is confirmed non-mutating (`git status` byte-identical
   before/after), but **any agent that appends an argument** changes that. Pin the literal string
   `npm run lint`, no interpolation. `npm run lint:fix` and `pwa-kit-dev format` are **forbidden**
   in the verify phase — an auto-format would erase the very prettier errors that make the 17-error
   count an invariant.
2. **`vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true`.** A typo'd path filter exits **0** having run
   nothing. **Assert on the reported test count, never on the exit code.**
3. **G3 and G5 exit non-zero at a healthy baseline** — lint exits 1 with its 17 pre-existing prettier
   errors, `audit:tokens` exits 1 with its 19. A loop that treats exit 0 as "pass" fails every
   iteration; one that treats non-zero as "fail" never passes. **Diff the counts, ignore the exit
   code.** Also: two pre-existing `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` lines on stderr from
   `theme/index.test.tsx` are noise on a *passing* suite — stderr is not failure.

- **Loop fit:** this is a *pre-flight prompt linter*, not a post-hoc diff checker. Correct call site is orchestrator → **before** dispatching each builder task, feeding it the task prompt. It will not score a completed change. Note `BLOCKED` is defined as "stop and get owner approval" — a human gate that will halt an unattended loop by design.

- **Reads:** `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `css.md`, `components.md`, `typescript.md`, `testing.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (when present).

Also it already spawns 4 subagents internally, so nesting it inside a scorer subagent gives you two levels of fan-out — budget for that.

### `pr-checklist` — retrospective / hand-off helper
Step 1 **invokes `/code-quality`** (nested skill call — mind the fan-out). Runs `git diff --name-only develop`, tiers each file, detects cross-squad PRs. Outputs a copy-paste PR description: summary bullets, file/tier/owner/reviewer table, required pre-merge actions, CodeRabbit gates (Conventional Commits title, Jira URL, JSDoc), test checklist. **Writes files:** no, and explicitly nothing is posted for you. Contains a hard constraint relevant to your tester: **"Claude must not start the dev server"** — `npm start` is a human action.

Sequential 5-step ritual. Reads in parallel: `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, `sprintScope.md`, `feedback.md`, `upstreamBaseline.md`, and `.claude/session-notes.md`. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md` (symlink target of `.claude/skills/code-review`). `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/1.0.0/`

- Session-isolated via `session_id`, so a loop in one session won't block another.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/settings.json`

1. **Inline branch guard — BLOCKING.** `exit 1` with "BLOCKED: You are on branch '$branch'…" if the current branch is `develop` or `main`. Your loop must be on a feature branch or every single edit fails.
2. `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` — non-blocking (always `exit 0`). Pattern-matches the target path and prints a Tier 2 owner warning (Global Shell = both squads; product components = Squad B; commerce components = Squad A; `theme/components/project/` = UI Designer; 8 named shared hooks = team RFC; translations = SI Partner). Noise in a loop, never a stopper.

**PostToolUse:**
1. `Write` → **Prettier `--write` on the new file.** `node_modules/.bin/prettier` via `jq -r '.tool_input.file_path'`. **This mutates the file your builder just wrote** — a scorer diffing against the builder's intended output will see formatting deltas.
2. `Edit|Write` → `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` — **file does not exist**; guarded by `[ -f … ] || true`, so it's a silent no-op.
3. `Edit|Write` → `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` — **mutates the repo.** For files under `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` (or `routes.tsx`), skipping `.test.`/`.stories.`/`ContentfulDefinition`, it runs `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs --file=<path>`, rewriting `.claude/registry/*.md`. It has a re-entry guard on `stop_hook_active`, and skips only when the working tree is clean.

> **Direct collision with `ralph-loop`.** Both register `Stop` hooks that return `decision: block`. In a build loop the tree is *never* clean, so `session-reflect` fires on every iteration, injecting a doc-writing task and an explicit "do not start new work" instruction into the exact turn `ralph-loop` is trying to re-prompt. `commit-msg` → `bash scripts/hooks/commit-msg "$1"`; `pre-commit` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit`; `pre-push` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-push`. Installed by `prepare: husky`; `core.hooksPath` = `.husky/_`.

Passes through `Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP`. **Every commit your loop makes must be Conventional Commits or it's rejected.** Note `upstream-sync` is a project-specific type, and the description is capped at 100 chars.

=== session-reflect.sh — when exactly does it fire? ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook: ask Claude to reflect on the session and draft proposals
# for AGENTS.md, .docs/memory/*, and any other docs that may have drifted.
# Proposals are written to .docs/agents-proposals/ — NEVER edits docs directly.
set -euo pipefail

input=$(cat)

# Re-entry guard: if a Stop hook already ran this turn, do nothing.
active=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false')
[ "$active" = "true" ] && exit 0

branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "no-branch")

# Skip only if nothing changed this session — otherwise always reflect,
# regardless of branch (develop/main/release included, just in case).
if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  exit 0

ts=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

# SFCC-89 — closed-loop execution workflow

**Planned 2026-08-26.** Supersedes this file's previous contents (the plan assurance pass, completed
2026-08-25 — its findings are recorded in `sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md`'s five changelogs).

---

## Context

The implementation plan is written, verified, and corrected. What is missing is a way to **execute**
it that does not rest on one agent's discipline holding across 5 commits.

Where we are:

- **The build already exists** — 29 staged files, 3,535 insertions, written 2026-08-24. tsc 0,
  Vitest 354/22, lint at develop's baseline, ACs verified against live SFCC. **Zero commits.**
- **The plan is a re-sequencing plan, not a build plan.** `AGENTS.md`'s copy-first rule requires the
  mechanical TypeScript port to land separately from the functional changes made on top; it got
  bundled (register row D5). With no commits the split is still free. After the first commit lands
  wrong, fixing it means rewriting history on a shared branch.
- **`sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md` is the spec** — 423 lines, 6 steps → 5 commits, per-step gates,
  five changelogs recording 16 verified corrections. **The loop executes it; it does not re-derive it.**
- **Step 0 is done.** Restore point `sfcc-89-wip` @ `3ae8dcd`, byte-exact (tree hash verified three
  times), never pushed. `git checkout sfcc-89-wip -- <path>` restores any single file.

Why a loop rather than just doing it: **Step 1 is a backwards reconstruction across 12 sites where no
gate can detect an omission.** The only mechanical signal is the lint *warning* count sitting at
exactly 15. A single pass that quietly misses three removal sites yields green tsc, green tests, an
unchanged error count, and a wrong commit. Independent verification and scoring is the mitigation.

## The goal, and its five authorities

Build SFCC-89 to spec — not under, not over. "Spec" is five things, and the scorer checks all five:

| # | Authority | Concretely |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The ticket** | Six enumerated fields (name, price, description, model copy, style code, ~~breadcrumb~~); "Contentful-sourced content" excluded; the `c_modelFit` dependency |
| 2 | **Figma** | `pdp/product-content` Desktop `40000307:14062` / Mobile `40000343:9727`; measured values only, frames/instances not TEXT nodes, no cross-file comparison |
| 3 | **The docs** | `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/*` — copy-first, minimal changes, tier rules, no new packages |
| 4 | **PR #59, now in develop** | The established precedent and this branch's base: camelCase `ui-kits/`, co-located `<name>.css.ts`, `var(--zimm-*)` in recipes not JSX, registered in `theme/components/index.ts` |
| 5 | **Token / component / CSS / override structure** | `textStyle` for type · `var(--zimm-*)` for colour+spacing · recipe per component · relative imports for already-overridden components · faithful default export on shared bridges |

## Role mapping — with one honest adjustment

**No custom agents exist in this repo or at user level** (`.claude/agents/` is absent in both). All
five roles are greenfield.

| Requested role | Implemented as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator + scope checker** | **The session (me)** | Only the session can dispatch subagents, hold state across iterations, run gates, and own the commit boundary. Already holds the plan, register and Jira context. |
| **Builder / implementer** | Fresh subagent per commit | Gets the step verbatim + the constraint set. Fresh, not a fork — so it cannot inherit my assumptions about what "done" looks like. |
| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Re-runs no gate I already ran; dispatches angle-specific sub-checks and consolidates. Keeps raw output out of my context. |
| **Scorer** | Fresh subagent, independent of builder | Gets diff + gate numbers + tester report + CodeRabbit findings + the 5-authority rubric. Returns PASS or REWORK with cited defects. |
| **Retrospective / meta** | Subagent at each boundary, fed a structured log | **The adjustment:** it cannot "listen while the loop runs" — subagents cannot observe each other's traffic, and only the session sees everything. So it is invoked at each boundary with an iteration log, and its output edits the *next* iteration's briefs. Same effect, one boundary of latency. |

Amendments persist to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/loop-briefs.md` so improvements accumulate across all 5
commits instead of being re-learned.

## Reuse, don't rebuild

Three existing skills cover parts of this. Their call sites differ and matter:

- **`/scope-check`** — a **pre-flight prompt linter**, not a diff auditor. Reads the tier rules and
  predicts what a prompt would touch, returning SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED and rewriting the prompt when
  needed. Correct call site: orchestrator, **before** dispatching each builder. Caveat: `BLOCKED`
  means "stop and get owner approval" — a deliberate human gate.
- **`/code-quality`** — a **post-hoc convention auditor** that already fans out to 4 parallel agents
  and emits a numeric `🔴 must-fix` count, a ready-made pass signal for the scorer. Two caveats: it
  **defaults its baseline to `main`** (we need `develop` — pin it explicitly), and it audits
  conventions, not behaviour, so the tester still owns the gates.
- **`/code-review`** (CodeRabbit CLI) — **mandated, not optional.** `AGENTS.md`'s Coding Task
  Workflow step 4: *"Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review…
  The CLI is required, not optional."* Verified available: **v0.7.5, authenticated, org
  ZimmermannAU, Pro, seat assigned.** Supports `--agent` (structured findings for agent workflows),
  `--light`, `--base`. This becomes **G7** below.

## The loop, per commit

```
  ORCHESTRATOR  pre-flight: restate the step's deliverables from the plan; confirm
                branch/HEAD/state; /scope-check the builder prompt before dispatch
        │
        ▼
  BUILDER       implement that step only → report changed files + rationale
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  run the deterministic gates myself (G1/G2/G3/G5) → capture real numbers
        │
        ▼
  TESTER        fan out to angle agents → consolidated findings (no gate re-runs)
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  G4 (Storybook) + G7 (CodeRabbit --agent) → structured findings
        │
        ▼
  SCORER        diff + gates + tester + CodeRabbit vs the 5-authority rubric
        │
        ├── REWORK ──► BUILDER (cited defects) ──► gates ──► TESTER ──► SCORER   [max 3]
        │                                                        │
        │                                          3rd REWORK ──► ESCALATE
        ▼
       PASS
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  scope re-check (under- AND over-delivery) → commit → G6 hard stop if due
        │
        ▼
  RETROSPECTIVE structured log → concrete brief edits → applied to the next commit
```

## Agent briefs

**Builder** (fresh, per commit) — gets the step verbatim; the 5-authority constraint set; the gate
numbers it must leave behind; the restore command; an explicit *do-not* list (no commits, no package
installs, no Tier 1 files, no `npm start`, no test-config edits, **never append args to
`npm run lint`**). Returns changed files with a one-line rationale each, plus anything it could not
do and why. **Never commits.**

**Tester** (per iteration) — gets the diff, the step's acceptance criteria, and the gate numbers
already measured. Fans out to four angles: (a) rules/tier compliance, (b) design-token and recipe
fidelity, (c) test/story coverage of this step's own contract, (d) base-parity regression — did
anything the plan did not name change? Returns findings with `file:line`, each CONFIRMED or
PLAUSIBLE, and **a mandatory "what I could not verify" section** — D17 survived eight invocations
because every pass reported only what it had checked.

**Scorer** (fresh, independent) — gets diff, gate numbers, tester report, CodeRabbit findings, the
step's plan text, the rubric. Returns per-axis PASS/REWORK with cited defects. Overall PASS only if
every axis passes **and** every gate number matches the plan exactly. **Must state what it tried to
falsify** — a PASS with no falsification attempt is not a PASS.

**Retrospective** (per boundary) — gets the iteration log: rework rounds, what the scorer caught,
what the tester missed that the scorer found (or vice versa), any gate surprise. Returns concrete
brief edits ("builder brief: add X to the do-not list"), not sentiments.

## The five commits

| | Subject | Steps | G6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `refactor(product-view): copy-first TypeScript port of product-view and product-detail` | 1 + 2 (+ `routes.tsx`, `vendor.d.ts`) | **hard stop** |
| 2 | `feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content` | 3 | — |
| 3 | `feat(ui-kits): add PDP static product information atoms and molecules` | 4a–4f | — |
| 4 | `feat(pdp): render static product information on the product detail page` | 5 | **hard stop** |
| 5 | `refactor(pdp): extract the static product header into a testable partial` | 6 | — |

## Gates — orchestrator-run, per commit

All 29 files stay on disk throughout; each commit selects contents **by path**. Timings measured on
this machine.

| | Command | Time | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 15s | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| G2 | `npx vitest run` | 15s | 354/22 | 354/22 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 |
| G3 | `npm run lint` | 15s | 17 err / **15 warn** | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 |
| G4 | Storybook interaction + a11y | ~2 min | 100/22 | 100/22 | 102/23 | 102/23 | 105/24 |
| G5 | `npm run audit:tokens` | 0.4s | 19→**14** | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| G7 | `cr review --light --agent --base develop` | ~1-3 min | required | required | required | required | required |
| G6 | Developer, live PDP | — | **stop** | — | — | **stop** | — |

**G3 is load-bearing at COMMIT 1** — the only signal that can catch a missed Step 1 removal.
Baseline 15, ceiling 25 if all 10 dead imports are left. Error count is a 17 invariant throughout.

**Inner loop (~45s, offline, zero repo writes)** — G1 → scoped G2 → G3 → G5. A scoped Vitest run is
**8× faster**: `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-detail` is 1.8s vs 15s. Full G2 before
every commit, always.

**G4 needs neither `http-server` nor `build-storybook`.** The CI recipe uses `npx http-server
storybook-static`, and `http-server` is genuinely absent from `package.json`, `node_modules`, and
global. But `test-storybook`'s default `--url` is already `http://127.0.0.1:6006` — exactly what
`npm run storybook` serves:

```
npm run storybook &                                    # dev server on 6006
npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 120000
node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci
```

Nothing written to `storybook-static/`, and incremental rebuilds between iterations instead of a
2-4 min cold build each time. `test-storybook`, `wait-on` and **Playwright's chromium
(`chromium-1223`) are all present** — verified, so no network needed. It is a long-lived background
process the loop must own and reap. Zero-dependency fallback: `python3 -m http.server 6006
--directory storybook-static`.

**G4 is more aggressive than it looks.** `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `a11y: { test: 'error' }`, so
**all 100 stories are a11y assertions**, not just the 37 carrying a `play`.

**Playwright is out of the loop entirely.** No PDP spec exists — `e2e/tests/` holds one file (two
homepage smoke tests). `ProductPage.js` scaffolding exists unused, there is no `e2e_pdp` allow-list
group, and change-scoping for our diff falls back to the full suite (those same two tests). Writing
one is blocked by a hard human gate: the Gherkin-first workflow requires Lead QA sign-off *before*
any Playwright code. Not a gap this loop can close.

**Two gates the loop is the sole enforcement for.** Neither `tsc --noEmit` nor `audit:tokens` is
wired into any CI workflow — `qa.yml` has no typecheck job. G1 and G5 are not extra diligence; they
are the only place those checks happen before merge.

## Loop hazards — hard-code these as guardrails

Five ways an automated loop silently corrupts its own signal here. All verified in source.

1. **`npm run lint` can be turned into a writer.** `package.json` has
   `"lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix"`, and `pwa-kit-dev lint` forwards `--`-args verbatim into a
   shell `execSync`. Plain `npm run lint` is confirmed non-mutating, but **any appended argument**
   changes that. Pin the literal string, no interpolation. `lint:fix` and `pwa-kit-dev format` are
   **forbidden** in the verify phase — auto-formatting would erase the very prettier errors that
   make the 17-error count an invariant.
2. **`vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true`.** A typo'd path filter exits **0** having run
   nothing. **Assert on the reported test count, never the exit code.**
3. **G3 and G5 exit non-zero at a healthy baseline** — lint exits 1 with its 17 pre-existing
   prettier errors, `audit:tokens` exits 1 with its 19. **Diff the counts; ignore the exit code.**
   Two pre-existing `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` stderr lines from `theme/index.test.tsx` are
   noise on a *passing* suite — stderr is not failure.
4. **`PostToolUse` hooks mutate what the builder wrote.** `Write` triggers `prettier --write` on the
   new file; `Edit|Write` triggers `registryUpdate.sh` → `generateRegistry.mjs --file=<path>`, which
   rewrites `.claude/registry/*.md` **on every single edit**. So registry churn appears in
   `git status` continuously, not just at commit time. The scorer must expect and ignore both.
5. **`.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` is a `Stop` hook that blocks on a dirty tree.** Verified: it
   returns `{"decision":"block"}` whenever `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, on any branch,
   instructing Claude to write a proposal to `.docs/agents-proposals/` and *"end the session — do
   not start new work."* It has a `stop_hook_active` re-entry guard. Our tree is never clean during
   the loop, so it fires at every turn boundary.

   **This is why the loop is orchestrator-driven and does not use the `ralph-loop` plugin.**
   `ralph-loop` drives iteration via its *own* `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` — two
   blocking Stop hooks racing on one turn with contradictory instructions. Fixing that would mean
   editing `.claude/settings.json`, which is **Tier 1**. Dispatching subagents from within a single
   orchestrator turn per commit sidesteps it entirely: the Stop hook then fires only at commit
   boundaries, where a pause is wanted anyway.

## Decisions settled by the developer, 2026-08-26

1. **All 5 commits pre-authorised** — the loop commits at each boundary, but *only* after the scorer
   returns PASS and the scope re-check clears. The five subjects above are the authorisation of
   record; anything else needs a fresh ask. Note `git add`/`commit`/`push` are not in either
   permissions allowlist, so commits may prompt — the scratch-branch commit did succeed earlier, so
   this is a verify-at-runtime item, not a blocker.
2. **Hard stop at both G6 points** — after COMMIT 1 and COMMIT 4. COMMIT 1's G6 proves the
   TypeScript override renders at all; everything after it assumes that.
3. **3 rework rounds per commit**, then escalate rather than loop again.
4. **Over-delivery is flagged, not auto-reverted** — anything beyond the plan's enumerated
   deliverables is reported with the diff, and the scorer withholds PASS until the developer rules.

## Termination and escalation

The loop stops — not retries — on any of:
- 3 rework rounds on one commit
- A gate number the plan does not predict that the scorer cannot explain
- Any Tier 1 path, `package.json`, or test-config file appearing in a diff
- `/scope-check` returning BLOCKED
- Scope divergence needing a developer ruling
- Either G6 hard stop
- `pre-commit` failing for a reason unrelated to the change (it has four independent `exit 1` paths)

## Verification — how we know the loop itself worked

1. `git diff sfcc-89-wip -- <the 29 paths>` shows **only** the plan's enumerated deltas.
2. Every commit's gate numbers match the table above, recorded per commit.
3. Every scorer PASS cites what it tried to falsify.
4. Every tester "could not verify" section is non-empty or explicitly reasoned empty.
5. `loop-briefs.md` shows at least one concrete brief amendment — a retrospective that changed
   nothing across 5 commits did not observe anything.
6. G7 ran on every commit, per `AGENTS.md`'s requirement, with each finding either fixed or
   explicitly dispositioned.

## What this does not do

- It does not re-plan. The realignment plan is the spec; disagreeing with it escalates, not forks.
- It does not push, open a PR, or write the PR body. The breadcrumb note is deferred and there is
  nothing to write it against yet.
- It does not resolve the four open items — `c_modelFit` (owner Dani, two-step), breadcrumb ACs
  (developer), open item (b) (scoped out), (d) SFCC-723, (e) PRC-12.
- It does not add PDP E2E coverage — human-gated, see Gates.
- It does not guarantee nothing is missed. D17 survived eight invocations of a comparable loop.

| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Re-runs no gate I already ran; dispatches angle-specific sub-checks and consolidates. Keeps raw output out of my context. |
| **Scorer** | Fresh subagent, independent of builder | Gets diff + gate numbers + tester report + CodeRabbit findings + the 5-authority rubric. Returns PASS or REWORK with cited defects. |

So it is invoked at each boundary with an iteration log, and its output edits the *next* iteration's briefs. Same effect, one boundary of latency. |

Amendments persist to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/loop-briefs.md` so improvements accumulate across all 5
commits instead of being re-learned.

## Reuse, don't rebuild

Three existing skills cover parts of this. Their call sites differ and matter:

- **`/scope-check`** — a **pre-flight prompt linter**, not a diff auditor. Reads the tier rules and
  predicts what a prompt would touch, returning SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED and rewriting the prompt when
  needed. Correct call site: orchestrator, **before** dispatching each builder. Caveat: `BLOCKED`
  means "stop and get owner approval" — a deliberate human gate.
- **`/code-quality`** — a **post-hoc convention auditor** that already fans out to 4 parallel agents
  and emits a numeric `🔴 must-fix` count, a ready-made pass signal for the scorer. Two caveats: it
  **defaults its baseline to `main`** (we need `develop` — pin it explicitly), and it audits
  conventions, not behaviour, so the tester still owns the gates.
- **`/code-review`** (CodeRabbit CLI) — **mandated, not optional.** `AGENTS.md`'s Coding Task
  Workflow step 4: *"Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review…
  The CLI is required, not optional."* Verified available: **v0.7.5, authenticated, org
  ZimmermannAU, Pro, seat assigned.** Supports `--agent` (structured findings for agent workflows),
  `--light`, `--base`. This becomes **G7** below.

## The loop, per commit

```
  ORCHESTRATOR  pre-flight: restate the step's deliverables from the plan; confirm
                branch/HEAD/state; /scope-check the builder prompt before dispatch
        │
        ▼
  BUILDER       implement that step only → report changed files + rationale
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  run the deterministic gates myself (G1/G2/G3/G5) → capture real numbers
        │
        ▼
  TESTER        fan out to angle agents → consolidated findings (no gate re-runs)
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  G4 (Storybook) + G7 (CodeRabbit --agent) → structured findings
        │
        ▼
  SCORER        diff + gates + tester + CodeRabbit vs the 5-authority rubric
        │
        ├── REWORK ──► BUILDER (cited defects) ──► gates ──► TESTER ──► SCORER   [max 3]
        │                                                        │
        │                                          3rd REWORK ──► ESCALATE
        ▼
       PASS
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  scope re-check (under- AND over-delivery) → commit → G6 hard stop if due
        │
        ▼
  RETROSPECTIVE structured log → concrete brief edits → applied to the next commit
```

## Agent briefs

**Builder** (fresh, per commit) — gets the step verbatim; the 5-authority constraint set; the gate
numbers it must leave behind; the restore command; an explicit *do-not* list (no commits, no package
installs, no Tier 1 files, no `npm start`, no test-config edits, **never append args to
`npm run lint`**). Returns changed files with a one-line rationale each, plus anything it could not
do and why. **Never commits.**

**Tester** (per iteration) — gets the diff, the step's acceptance criteria, and the gate numbers
already measured. Fans out to four angles: (a) rules/tier compliance, (b) design-token and recipe
fidelity, (c) test/story coverage of this step's own contract, (d) base-parity regression — did
anything the plan did not name change? Returns findings with `file:line`, each CONFIRMED or
PLAUSIBLE, and **a mandatory "what I could not verify" section** — D17 survived eight invocations
because every pass reported only what it had checked.

**Scorer** (fresh, independent) — gets diff, gate numbers, tester report, CodeRabbit findings, the
step's plan text, the rubric. Returns per-axis PASS/REWORK with cited defects. Overall PASS only if
every axis passes **and** every gate number matches the plan exactly. **Must state what it tried to
falsify** — a PASS with no falsification attempt is not a PASS.

**Retrospective** (per boundary) — gets the iteration log: rework rounds, what the scorer caught,
what the tester missed that the scorer found (or vice versa), any gate surprise. Returns concrete
brief edits ("builder brief: add X to the do-not list"), not sentiments.

## The five commits

| | Subject | Steps | G6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `refactor(product-view): copy-first TypeScript port of product-view and product-detail` | 1 + 2 (+ `routes.tsx`, `vendor.d.ts`) | **hard stop** |
| 2 | `feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content` | 3 | — |
| 3 | `feat(ui-kits): add PDP static product information atoms and molecules` | 4a–4f | — |
| 4 | `feat(pdp): render static product information on the product detail page` | 5 | **hard stop** |
| 5 | `refactor(pdp): extract the static product header into a testable partial` | 6 | — |

## Gates — orchestrator-run, per commit

All 29 files stay on disk throughout; each commit selects contents **by path**. Timings measured on
this machine.

| | Command | Time | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 15s | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| G2 | `npx vitest run` | 15s | 354/22 | 354/22 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 |
| G3 | `npm run lint` | 15s | 17 err / **15 warn** | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 |
| G4 | Storybook interaction + a11y | ~2 min | 100/22 | 100/22 | 102/23 | 102/23 | 105/24 |
| G5 | `npm run audit:tokens` | 0.4s | 19→**14** | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| G7 | `cr review --light --agent --base develop` | ~1-3 min | required | required | required | required | required |
| G6 | Developer, live PDP | — | **stop** | — | — | **stop** | — |

**G3 is load-bearing at COMMIT 1** — the only signal that can catch a missed Step 1 removal.
Baseline 15, ceiling 25 if all 10 dead imports are left. Error count is a 17 invariant throughout.

**Inner loop (~45s, offline, zero repo writes)** — G1 → scoped G2 → G3 → G5. A scoped Vitest run is
**8× faster**: `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-detail` is 1.8s vs 15s. Full G2 before
every commit, always.

**G4 needs neither `http-server` nor `build-storybook`.** The CI recipe uses `npx http-server
storybook-static`, and `http-server` is genuinely absent from `package.json`, `node_modules`, and
global. But `test-storybook`'s default `--url` is already `http://127.0.0.1:6006` — exactly what
`npm run storybook` serves:

```
npm run storybook &                                    # dev server on 6006
npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 120000
node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci
```

Nothing written to `storybook-static/`, and incremental rebuilds between iterations instead of a
2-4 min cold build each time. `test-storybook`, `wait-on` and **Playwright's chromium
(`chromium-1223`) are all present** — verified, so no network needed. It is a long-lived background
process the loop must own and reap. Zero-dependency fallback: `python3 -m http.server 6006
--directory storybook-static`.

**G4 is more aggressive than it looks.** `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `a11y: { test: 'error' }`, so
**all 100 stories are a11y assertions**, not just the 37 carrying a `play`.

**Playwright is out of the loop entirely.** No PDP spec exists — `e2e/tests/` holds one file (two
homepage smoke tests). `ProductPage.js` scaffolding exists unused, there is no `e2e_pdp` allow-list
group, and change-scoping for our diff falls back to the full suite (those same two tests). Writing
one is blocked by a hard human gate: the Gherkin-first workflow requires Lead QA sign-off *before*
any Playwright code. Not a gap this loop can close.

**Two gates the loop is the sole enforcement for.** Neither `tsc --noEmit` nor `audit:tokens` is
wired into any CI workflow — `qa.yml` has no typecheck job. G1 and G5 are not extra diligence; they
are the only place those checks happen before merge.

## Loop hazards — hard-code these as guardrails

Five ways an automated loop silently corrupts its own signal here. All verified in source.

1. **`npm run lint` can be turned into a writer.** `package.json` has
   `"lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix"`, and `pwa-kit-dev lint` forwards `--`-args verbatim into a
   shell `execSync`. Plain `npm run lint` is confirmed non-mutating, but **any appended argument**
   changes that. Pin the literal string, no interpolation. `lint:fix` and `pwa-kit-dev format` are
   **forbidden** in the verify phase — auto-formatting would erase the very prettier errors that
   make the 17-error count an invariant.
2. **`vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true`.** A typo'd path filter exits **0** having run
   nothing. **Assert on the reported test count, never the exit code.**
3. **G3 and G5 exit non-zero at a healthy baseline** — lint exits 1 with its 17 pre-existing
   prettier errors, `audit:tokens` exits 1 with its 19. **Diff the counts; ignore the exit code.**
   Two pre-existing `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` stderr lines from `theme/index.test.tsx` are
   noise on a *passing* suite — stderr is not failure.
4. **`PostToolUse` hooks mutate what the builder wrote.** `Write` triggers `prettier --write` on the
   new file; `Edit|Write` triggers `registryUpdate.sh` → `generateRegistry.mjs --file=<path>`, which
   rewrites `.claude/registry/*.md` **on every single edit**. So registry churn appears in
   `git status` continuously, not just at commit time. The scorer must expect and ignore both.
5. **`.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` is a `Stop` hook that blocks on a dirty tree.** Verified: it
   returns `{"decision":"block"}` whenever `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, on any branch,
   instructing Claude to write a proposal to `.docs/agents-proposals/` and *"end the session — do
   not start new work."* It has a `stop_hook_active` re-entry guard. Our tree is never clean during
   the loop, so it fires at every turn boundary.

   **This is why the loop is orchestrator-driven and does not use the `ralph-loop` plugin.**
   `ralph-loop` drives iteration via its *own* `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` — two
   blocking Stop hooks racing on one turn with contradictory instructions. Fixing that would mean
   editing `.claude/settings.json`, which is **Tier 1**. Dispatching subagents from within a single
   orchestrator turn per commit sidesteps it entirely: the Stop hook then fires only at commit
   boundaries, where a pause is wanted anyway.

## Decisions settled by the developer, 2026-08-26

1. **All 5 commits pre-authorised** — the loop commits at each boundary, but *only* after the scorer
   returns PASS and the scope re-check clears. The five subjects above are the authorisation of
   record; anything else needs a fresh ask. Note `git add`/`commit`/`push` are not in either
   permissions allowlist, so commits may prompt — the scratch-branch commit did succeed earlier, so
   this is a verify-at-runtime item, not a blocker.
2. **Hard stop at both G6 points** — after COMMIT 1 and COMMIT 4. COMMIT 1's G6 proves the
   TypeScript override renders at all; everything after it assumes that.
3. **3 rework rounds per commit**, then escalate rather than loop again.
4. **Over-delivery is flagged, not auto-reverted** — anything beyond the plan's enumerated
   deliverables is reported with the diff, and the scorer withholds PASS until the developer rules.

## Termination and escalation

The loop stops — not retries — on any of:
- 3 rework rounds on one commit
- A gate number the plan does not predict that the scorer cannot explain
- Any Tier 1 path, `package.json`, or test-config file appearing in a diff
- `/scope-check` returning BLOCKED
- Scope divergence needing a developer ruling
- Either G6 hard stop
- `pre-commit` failing for a reason unrelated to the change (it has four independent `exit 1` paths)

## Verification — how we know the loop itself worked

1. `git diff sfcc-89-wip -- <the 29 paths>` shows **only** the plan's enumerated deltas.
2. Every commit's gate numbers match the table above, recorded per commit.
3. Every scorer PASS cites what it tried to falsify.
4. Every tester "could not verify" section is non-empty or explicitly reasoned empty.
5. `loop-briefs.md` shows at least one concrete brief amendment — a retrospective that changed
   nothing across 5 commits did not observe anything.
6. G7 ran on every commit, per `AGENTS.md`'s requirement, with each finding either fixed or
   explicitly dispositioned.

## What this does not do

- It does not re-plan. The realignment plan is the spec; disagreeing with it escalates, not forks.
- It does not push, open a PR, or write the PR body. The breadcrumb note is deferred and there is
  nothing to write it against yet.
- It does not resolve the four open items — `c_modelFit` (owner Dani, two-step), breadcrumb ACs
  (developer), open item (b) (scoped out), (d) SFCC-723, (e) PRC-12.
- It does not add PDP E2E coverage — human-gated, see Gates.
- It does not guarantee nothing is missed. D17 survived eight invocations of a comparable loop.

**Planned 2026-08-26.** Supersedes this file's previous contents (the plan assurance pass, completed
2026-08-25 — its findings are recorded in `sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md`'s five changelogs).

---

## Context

The implementation plan is written, verified, and corrected. What is missing is a way to **execute**
it that does not rest on one agent's discipline holding across 5 commits.

Where we are:

- **The build already exists** — 29 staged files, 3,535 insertions, written 2026-08-24. tsc 0,
  Vitest 354/22, lint at develop's baseline, ACs verified against live SFCC. **Zero commits.**
- **The plan is a re-sequencing plan, not a build plan.** `AGENTS.md`'s copy-first rule requires the
  mechanical TypeScript port to land separately from the functional changes made on top; it got
  bundled (register row D5). With no commits the split is still free. After the first commit lands
  wrong, fixing it means rewriting history on a shared branch.
- **`sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md` is the spec** — 423 lines, 6 steps → 5 commits, per-step gates,
  five changelogs recording 16 verified corrections. **The loop executes it; it does not re-derive it.**
- **Step 0 is done.** Restore point `sfcc-89-wip` @ `3ae8dcd`, byte-exact (tree hash verified three
  times), never pushed. `git checkout sfcc-89-wip -- <path>` restores any single file.

Why a loop rather than just doing it: **Step 1 is a backwards reconstruction across 12 sites where no
gate can detect an omission.** The only mechanical signal is the lint *warning* count sitting at
exactly 15. A single pass that quietly misses three removal sites yields green tsc, green tests, an
unchanged error count, and a wrong commit. Independent verification and scoring is the mitigation.

## The goal, and its five authorities

Build SFCC-89 to spec — not under, not over. "Spec" is five things, and the scorer checks all five:

| # | Authority | Concretely |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The ticket** | Six enumerated fields (name, price, description, model copy, style code, ~~breadcrumb~~); "Contentful-sourced content" excluded; the `c_modelFit` dependency |
| 2 | **Figma** | `pdp/product-content` Desktop `40000307:14062` / Mobile `40000343:9727`; measured values only, frames/instances not TEXT nodes, no cross-file comparison |
| 3 | **The docs** | `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/*` — copy-first, minimal changes, tier rules, no new packages |
| 4 | **PR #59, now in develop** | The established precedent and this branch's base: camelCase `ui-kits/`, co-located `<name>.css.ts`, `var(--zimm-*)` in recipes not JSX, registered in `theme/components/index.ts` |
| 5 | **Token / component / CSS / override structure** | `textStyle` for type · `var(--zimm-*)` for colour+spacing · recipe per component · relative imports for already-overridden components · faithful default export on shared bridges |

## Role mapping — with one honest adjustment

**No custom agents exist in this repo or at user level** (`.claude/agents/` is absent in both). All
five roles are greenfield.

| Requested role | Implemented as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator + scope checker** | **The session (me)** | Only the session can dispatch subagents, hold state across iterations, run gates, and own the commit boundary. Already holds the plan, register and Jira context. |
| **Builder / implementer** | Fresh subagent per commit | Gets the step verbatim + the constraint set. Fresh, not a fork — so it cannot inherit my assumptions about what "done" looks like. |
| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Re-runs no gate I already ran; dispatches angle-specific sub-checks and consolidates. Keeps raw output out of my context. |
| **Scorer** | Fresh subagent, independent of builder | Gets diff + gate numbers + tester report + CodeRabbit findings + the 5-authority rubric. Returns PASS or REWORK with cited defects. |
| **Retrospective / meta** | Subagent at each boundary, fed a structured log | **The adjustment:** it cannot "listen while the loop runs" — subagents cannot observe each other's traffic, and only the session sees everything. So it is invoked at each boundary with an iteration log, and its output edits the *next* iteration's briefs. Same effect, one boundary of latency. |

Amendments persist to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/loop-briefs.md` so improvements accumulate across all 5
commits instead of being re-learned.

## Reuse, don't rebuild

Three existing skills cover parts of this. Their call sites differ and matter:

- **`/scope-check`** — a **pre-flight prompt linter**, not a diff auditor. Reads the tier rules and
  predicts what a prompt would touch, returning SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED and rewriting the prompt when
  needed. Correct call site: orchestrator, **before** dispatching each builder. Caveat: `BLOCKED`
  means "stop and get owner approval" — a deliberate human gate.
- **`/code-quality`** — a **post-hoc convention auditor** that already fans out to 4 parallel agents
  and emits a numeric `🔴 must-fix` count, a ready-made pass signal for the scorer. Two caveats: it
  **defaults its baseline to `main`** (we need `develop` — pin it explicitly), and it audits
  conventions, not behaviour, so the tester still owns the gates.
- **`/code-review`** (CodeRabbit CLI) — **mandated, not optional.** `AGENTS.md`'s Coding Task
  Workflow step 4: *"Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review…
  The CLI is required, not optional."* Verified available: **v0.7.5, authenticated, org
  ZimmermannAU, Pro, seat assigned.** Supports `--agent` (structured findings for agent workflows),
  `--light`, `--base`. This becomes **G7** below.

## The loop, per commit

```
  ORCHESTRATOR  pre-flight: restate the step's deliverables from the plan; confirm
                branch/HEAD/state; /scope-check the builder prompt before dispatch
        │
        ▼
  BUILDER       implement that step only → report changed files + rationale
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  run the deterministic gates myself (G1/G2/G3/G5) → capture real numbers
        │
        ▼
  TESTER        fan out to angle agents → consolidated findings (no gate re-runs)
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  G4 (Storybook) + G7 (CodeRabbit --agent) → structured findings
        │
        ▼
  SCORER        diff + gates + tester + CodeRabbit vs the 5-authority rubric
        │

43	## Role mapping — with one honest adjustment
44	
45	**No custom agents exist in this repo or at user level** (`.claude/agents/` is absent in both). All
46	five roles are greenfield.
47	
48	| Requested role | Implemented as | Why |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| **Orchestrator + scope checker** | **The session (me)** | Only the session can dispatch subagents, hold state across iterations, run gates, and own the commit boundary. Already holds the plan, register and Jira context. |

52	| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Re-runs no gate I already ran; dispatches angle-specific sub-checks and consolidates. Keeps raw output out of my context. |

So it is invoked at each boundary with an iteration log, and its output edits the *next* iteration's briefs. Same effect, one boundary of latency. |

content.text:
All retrospective fixes applied. **COMMIT 1 is done and I'm holding for your G6.**

## The retrospective found a live bug in my own tooling

The spec extract I handed the builder was written at **01:32**; I corrected the plan at **01:46**. So the builder was working from a file that still said `G3: 17 err / 15 warn, ceiling 25` — **the exact stale number that became cross-correction #1.** It also duplicated Step 1 and leaked Step 3's heading.

The builder caught the discrepancy on its own. Had it not, we'd have chased a phantom warning all the way to a REWORK.

**Fixed properly:** the extractor is now a verified contiguous slice — it stamps the plan's sha256 and mtime into the header, then proves every non-blank line exists verbatim in the plan and fails loudly if not. COMMIT 2's slice is built and confirmed carrying the **current** figure (16, not 15).

## Ten things in the plans were provably wrong

The headline ones, all now corrected:

- **My workflow plan still had G3 at 15 for all five commits.** I'd fixed the realignment plan but not this one — and this one is what I read. Now 16 at C1–C2, 15 from C3, ceiling 26.
- **Both carry-forwards were assigned to the wrong commit.** Neither `product-view` nor `product-detail` is in COMMIT 3's path set, so actioning them there would have broken commit-by-path discipline. Re-homed: the inert `cloneElement` casts and the `ProductViewRefScope` JSDoc → **COMMIT 2**; the `as unknown as React.Ref` → **COMMIT 4**.
- **The G4 static shortcut is void at COMMIT 3 and COMMIT 5.** Both rewrite files *inside* the story import graph — running against a stale build would render the old components and report a green 100/22 while exercising nothing new. Now conditional, with the grep that decides it.
- **Step 3's citation `:13-17` is stale** — the sentence it quotes is at `:19`. Editing blind would have rewritten the wrong paragraph.
- **G4's baseline provenance was a coincidence, not a cross-check.** `index.json` holds 101 entries — 100 `story` + 1 `docs`. The `^export const` count landing on 100 too is two different measures agreeing by accident.

## What the loop is structurally blind to

Worth stating plainly, because all eight cross-corrections were the *same class*: static, textual, internal-consistency errors. Every role reads the same text, so the loop is excellent at those and has no instrument for:

**Rendered behaviour.** Neither Storybook nor Vitest loads the `ccExtensibility` resolver — so a base-path import inside an override renders the *base* component in both, and the *override* in the app. No gate distinguishes them.

**Spatial correctness.** A recipe applying the right token to the wrong property — `paddingBottom` instead of `paddingTop` — passes every gate including the `play`. Nothing measures anything against Figma.

**Cross-commit fit.** COMMIT 2 adds a prop with zero consumers; COMMIT 3 builds components nothing renders. A `renderHeader` signature that doesn't match what Step 5 needs passes both cleanly.

Its conclusion on the shape: **don't add a fifth reviewer.** Two independent readers both read past the false "unavoidable" comment; a third would too. What caught it was a builder *action* — deleting the cast and re-running tsc. So the budget goes into mandatory falsification actions, not more readers.

## Recommended shape change for COMMIT 3

Split the builder at the natural seam. **4e is subtractive across 8 sites and is the only thing moving G3's warning count 16 → 15** — run together with the additive work, a 15 could mean "4e complete" or "4e incomplete plus an accidental fix". Dispatch 4e alone first, gate it at exactly `17/15` and `353/22`, then the additive work. Same isolation Step 1 got, same reason.

## Your G6

**http://localhost:3000/product/8637DS241** — should look **exactly as before any of this work**. Base PDP, no Zimmermann static-info column, no model line, no style code.

That's five orchestrator errors plus two gate-configuration defects. The loop isn't finding these because the agents are clever — it's finding them because every claim gets checked against the file by someone who didn't make it.

Tester's still running its four re-pointed angles. I'll fold in both G7 runs and the tester before the scorer sees any of it.

**G7 now genuinely covers COMMIT 3: 33 files, all 7 new ones visible, 0 findings.**

That's the first honest pre-commit CodeRabbit review in this whole loop. The previous three were all reading state that didn't include the work being reviewed.

## The full picture of the G7 defect

Three invocations, three different answers on the same code:

| Invocation | Files | Findings | What it actually read |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base develop` | 33 | 1 | **staged state** — flagged D1, already fixed in the worktree |
| `--uncommitted` | 26 | 0 | tracked edits only — **blind to all 7 new files** |
| `--uncommitted` + intent-to-add | **33** | **0** | the real change, including the new molecule |

The middle row is the trap worth remembering: a clean 0 that looked like a pass, while the most novel code in the commit — the entire `zimmProductMeta` molecule, both new recipes, the new test — was never examined.

I used `git add -N` to fix it: intent-to-add makes the files tracked without staging content, so the index stays honest and it's reversible with `git rm --cached`. Verified tsc still 0 afterwards.

## Where COMMIT 3 stands

| Gate | Required | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | 0 | **0** |
| G2 | 354+P+M / 24 | **362 / 24** |
| G3 | 17 err / 15 warn | **17 / 15** |
| G4 | 102 / 23 | **102 / 23** (8s, isolated port) |
| G5 | 14 unack / 22 ack | **14 / 22** |
| G7 | must run | **0 findings / 33 files**, properly scoped |

Every arithmetic prediction landed. Waiting on the tester's four re-pointed angles — the gate-observability one, where it deletes each new artefact to find which gate actually notices, and the cross-commit-fit one checking COMMIT 3's prop surfaces against what Step 5 will hand them.

That second angle is the loop's known structural blind spot, so it's the one I'm most interested in. A mismatch there passes COMMIT 3 and COMMIT 4 independently and only surfaces at your G6.

<result>Full suite green (24 files / 362 tests) on the clean copy. Here are the findings.

## Premise corrections (both matter for the caller)

The WIP ref I used is **`sfcc-89-wip`** (commit `3ae8dcd` "chore: wip SFCC-89 static product info restore point"), branched off `8362b3c`. Two of the task's stated premises do not match what's actually on that ref:

1. **COMMIT 4 does not use the ternary.** `/tmp/wip_pdp.tsx` ← `sfcc-89-wip:overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:730` — anchor `<ZimmProductContent name={info.name} headingLevel="h2" price={info.price} description={info.description} />`. `isProductPartOfBundle` *is* destructured (`:713`, anchor `isProductPartOfBundle,`) but only gates the PromoCallout (`:734`, anchor `{!isProductPartOfBundle && (`). No `undefined` ternary reaches `price`.
2. **COMMIT 4 does not use `ZimmProductMeta` at all** — the molecule does not exist on that ref. The page renders the two atoms directly: `:882` anchor `<ZimmProductModelInfo modelInfo={staticInfo?.modelInfo} />` and `:883` anchor `<ZimmProductStyleCode value={staticInfo?.styleCode} />`, wrapped in `:881` anchor `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">`.

---

## 1. Explicit `undefined` through the optional chain — CONFIRMED SAFE (NOTE)

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/tsconfig.json` — no `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and **no `extends` key at all** (grep returned nothing); `find` confirms it is the only `tsconfig*.json` outside `node_modules`, so there is no base config from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev` in play.

**Experiment.** In `/tmp/c3probe/xfit` I wrote `overrides/app/__xfit_pos.tsx` passing (a) literal `undefined`, (b) a `string | undefined` union, and (c) the exact premise ternary `isBundle ? undefined : info.price` into both `ZimmProductContent` and `ZimmProductPrice`, plus mapper output into `ZimmProductMeta`/`ZimmProductStyleCode`/`ZimmProductModelInfo`. Result: `TSC_EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics.

**Negative control (proves tsc was reading the scratch file):** `overrides/app/__xfit_neg.tsx` passing `undefined` to non-optional props produced `TSC_EXIT=2` and exactly 4 errors:
```
overrides/app/__xfit_neg.tsx(8,45): error TS2322: Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'.
overrides/app/__xfit_neg.tsx(10,54): error TS2322: Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type '"h1" | "h2" | "h3"'.
overrides/app/__xfit_neg.tsx(12,51): error TS2322: Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type '"h1" | "h2" | "h3"'.
overrides/app/__xfit_neg.tsx(14,45): error TS2322: Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'.
```

**Decisive cross-commit experiment.** Copied `sfcc-89-wip`'s page onto COMMIT 3's working-tree components → `TSC_EXIT=0`. Then mutated it into the *expected* COMMIT 4 shape (`price={isProductPartOfBundle ? undefined : info.price}` **and** the atoms swapped for `<ZimmProductMeta modelInfo={staticInfo?.modelInfo} styleCode={staticInfo?.styleCode} />`) → `TSC_EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics. **The prop surfaces fit; there is no type-level cross-commit break.**

### Runtime guard `if (!price) return null` — CONFIRMED correct, no wrongly-hidden value
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:35` — anchor `if (!price) return null;`. Rendered a matrix through real jsdom:
```
PRICE | ""        | rendered=false
PRICE | "0"       | rendered=true  text="0"
PRICE | "0.00"    | rendered=true  text="0.00"
PRICE | "$0.00"   | rendered=true  text="$0.00"
PRICE | " "       | rendered=true  text=" "
PRICE | "$NaN"    | rendered=true  text="$NaN"
```
`price` is typed `string`, so numeric `0` is unreachable (the negative control shows tsc enforces this). `'0'`/`'0.00'`/`'$0.00'` all render — **there is no value where `!price` is true but hiding is wrong.** My hypothesis that a zero price would be wrongly hidden is **falsified**.

---

## 2. `ZimmProductMeta` prop surface vs what the page will pass

### 2a. BLOCKER-adjacent — `ZimmProductMeta` has zero consumers (CONFIRMED, DEFECT)
`grep -rn "ZimmProductMeta" overrides/` returns only its own folder plus one registration: `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:38` — anchor `ZimmProductMeta,`. COMMIT 4 as it exists on `sfcc-89-wip` renders the two atoms directly and **will not pick the molecule up**. So COMMIT 3 ships a molecule + recipe + 4-case Vitest suite + Storybook `play` that nothing renders, and COMMIT 4 must be *edited* beyond a restore to consume it. The loop scores each commit alone, so neither diff surfaces this.

### 2b. Field names and types line up exactly (CONFIRMED)
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:33-39` — anchor `export type PdpProductInfo = {` — produces `modelInfo?: string` (`:60`, anchor `modelInfo: product.c_modelFit,`) and `styleCode?: string` (`:64`, anchor `styleCode: product.master?.masterId ?? product.id,`). `ZimmProductMeta`'s props (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductMeta/index.tsx:14` anchor `modelInfo?: string;`, `:19` anchor `styleCode?: string;`) match name-for-name and type-for-type. No adaptation needed — proven by the tsc run above.

Correction to the task's premise: **the mapper does *not* normalise `modelInfo`/`styleCode` to `''`.** Only `price` is normalised (`:58`, anchor `price: typeof priceData?.currentPrice === 'number' ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, currency) : '',`). The other three pass through raw, so `string | undefined`.

`ZimmProductStyleCode`'s `value` was **already** optional on the WIP baseline (`git show sfcc-89-wip:...zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:14` → `value?: string;`), so no tsc error there — confirmed by compiling, not reading.

### 2c. Guard predicate is consistent — my "empty padded box" hypothesis FALSIFIED (CONFIRMED)
`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:227` — anchor `export const isBlankRichText = (html?: string | null): boolean => richTextToPlainText(html).trim() === '';`. Measured across every mapper-producible input:
```
isBlankRichText(undefined)          -> true
isBlankRichText('')                 -> true
isBlankRichText('<p></p>')          -> true   (nodeCount=1, plain="")
isBlankRichText('<p> </p>')         -> true
isBlankRichText('<br>')             -> true
isBlankRichText('&nbsp;')           -> true
isBlankRichText('<ul><li></li></ul>')-> true
isBlankRichText('<p>Model is 178cm</p>') -> false
```
So `''` and `'<p></p>'` both return `true`. The molecule's guard (`.../zimmProductMeta/index.tsx:43`, anchor `if (isBlankRichText(modelInfo) && !styleCode) return null;`) is **exactly the conjunction** of the two children's own guards (`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:29` anchor `if (isBlankRichText(modelInfo)) return null;` and `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:29` anchor `if (!value) return null;`). I probed for a rendered-root-with-no-children case and my "EMPTY PADDED BOX REPRODUCED" marker never fired.

### 2d. Guard asymmetry: whitespace-only style code renders a bare label (CONFIRMED, NOTE)
The one inconsistency I could reproduce — the modelInfo side is whitespace-aware, the styleCode side is bare-falsy:
```
META | styleCode whitespace only  | root=true | model=false | code=true | rootText="Style Code:    "
```
A `styleCode` of `'   '` renders the label `Style Code:` with no value, and drags the whole 28px block onto the page. Whether SFCC can emit a whitespace-only `master.masterId`/`id` I could not establish, so this is a latent asymmetry rather than a live bug. Note also `??` at `productInfo.ts:64` does **not** fall through on `''` — an empty-string `masterId` is returned as `''` rather than falling back to `product.id`; that one collapses correctly, so it's benign today.

---

## 3. Did widening `price` break existing consumers/stories? — CONFIRMED NO

Baseline for "pre-existing" is `sfcc-89-wip`. There are **four** pre-existing stories, not three:
```
sfcc-89-wip: Default(38) WithoutDescription(47) RhythmWithDescription(70) BlankDescription(92)
worktree:    Default(38) WithoutDescription(47) RhythmWithDescription(70) BlankDescription(92) WithoutPrice(109)
```
`git diff sfcc-89-wip -- .../zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx` is **purely additive** — the only change is the new `WithoutPrice` block appended after line 105. All four pre-existing stories are byte-identical and all pass a truthy `price: '$795.00'`, so **none silently falls into the new null-return branch**:
- `:62` anchor `await expect(root.children).toHaveLength(2);` (name + price, description collapsed) — still 2. ✔
- `:80` anchor `await expect(root.children).toHaveLength(3);` — still 3. ✔
- `:104` anchor `await expect(canvas.getByTestId('product-content').children).toHaveLength(2);` — still 2. ✔
- No pre-existing `play` asserts anything about `product-price`; the only such assertion is inside the **new** story (`:126`, anchor `await expect(canvas.queryByTestId('product-price')).not.toBeInTheDocument();`).

The new branch **is** covered at both layers: the `WithoutPrice` story above, plus a new untracked Vitest file `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx:24` — anchor `test.each([undefined, ''])('renders nothing for %s', (price) => {`.

**No blank-canvas trap in the price atom's stories.** `git diff sfcc-89-wip -- .../zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx` is empty (unchanged), and both stories pass truthy values: `:20` anchor `args: { price: '$795.00' },` and `:29-32` anchors `<ZimmProductPrice price="$795.00" />` … `<ZimmProductPrice price="HK$6,200.00" />`. Nothing renders an empty canvas.

Full suite on the clean copy: **24 files / 362 tests, all passing.**

---

## Two further cross-commit findings the per-diff loop cannot see

### A. Double top-padding if COMMIT 4 swaps the molecule into the existing Stack (CONFIRMED values, PLAUSIBLE trigger)
`sfcc-89-wip:.../product-detail/index.tsx:881` — anchor `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">`. `overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts:14` — anchor `l:     '1.25rem',  // 20px`. The molecule's own recipe adds its own: `.../zimmProductMeta/zimmProductMeta.css.ts:22` anchor `const SPACE_META_ROW = '1.75rem'; // 28px at the default 16px root`, applied at `:35` anchor `paddingTop: SPACE_META_ROW, // drawers -> model line`. The two sit on different elements, so a naive swap that keeps the `Stack` yields **20px + 28px = 48px** against a design that specifies 28px — and the molecule's `play` (`.../zimmProductMeta/index.stories.tsx:53`, anchor `await expect(getComputedStyle(root).paddingTop).toBe('28px');`) measures the molecule in isolation and would still pass. The `Stack` must be deleted, not repopulated.

### B. The `typeof === 'number'` price guard admits `NaN` and `Infinity` (CONFIRMED behaviour, unproven reachability, NOTE)
`productInfo.ts:58` — anchor `price: typeof priceData?.currentPrice === 'number' ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, currency) : '',`. Since `typeof NaN === 'number'`:

## The catch that matters most: COMMIT 4 would have shipped the molecule dead

`ZimmProductMeta` currently has **no consumer**. And COMMIT 4 is a *restore* — the block sitting in `sfcc-89-wip` renders the two atoms directly:

```
:881  <Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">
:882    <ZimmProductModelInfo … />
:883    <ZimmProductStyleCode … />
```

So a faithful restore ships everything COMMIT 3 built **unused**, and the 28px D15 fix never reaches the page.

Worse is the near-miss version: keep the `Stack` *and* put the molecule inside it, and you get the Stack's 20px plus the molecule's own 28px = **48px against a 28px spec**. The molecule's `play` measures `paddingTop` in isolation, reads 28px, and passes. Every other gate is blind. Only a human looking at the page would catch it.

**The `Stack` must be deleted, not repopulated.** That's now written into the COMMIT 4 brief.

This is precisely the structural blind spot the retrospective identified — each commit scored against one diff, nothing checking commit N against commit N+1's requirements. Re-pointing the tester's angles at cross-commit fit is what surfaced it.

## Two builder claims were false

"All 19 registered keys asserted programmatically" — **no test asserts any specific key**. And "both new test files mutation-proven" was half true: `zimmProductMeta` had **three surviving mutations** — swap the children, drop a prop forwarding, pass the wrong argument to the guard — because it used input-insensitive `mockReturnValue`. The state space was fully covered; the prop→state mapping wasn't covered at all.

## And one defect is mine

I told the builder to use `rowGap` because "a real browser expands the shorthand", and that jsdom made the assertion impossible in Vitest. **Both halves are false** — I measured it: Chromium returns `gap: "28px"`, and jsdom under a `ChakraProvider` returns `gap="1.75rem"`.

The cost wasn't the property name. It's that the resulting comment tells future readers **recipe-resolution assertions are impossible in Vitest** — which is exactly the fix the unobservable-recipe defect needs. A false comment doesn't just misinform, it forecloses the right solution.

Six of my errors caught by subagents now; this is the first that propagated into shipped code. New standing rule: never assert runtime behaviour in a brief without measuring it first, or mark it `CLAIMED` and let the builder verify.

was still a flex item, so a product with no price got two 20px gaps with nothing between them. The atom now returns null after its hook — the guard must sit below useStyleConfig or the hook call becomes conditional, which is a lint error, not a warning. The meta block rendered an empty padded box for every product with neither model copy nor a style code, which is every product while the page loads. It now collapses. The guard is load-bearing rather than defensive: the recipe carries paddingTop, and padding renders unconditionally, so a wrapper with two null children still occupies space. The house pattern elsewhere needs no guard precisely because it uses gap and no padding. The design specifies 28px between the drawers and the model line, and again between the model line and the style code. Both hops now come from one constant, matching the pattern theme/components/footer.ts already uses for a shared section value. 28px has no rem-valued token. --zimm-scale-700 holds 28px but as a raw px string, so substituting it would convert scaling spacing into fixed spacing and regress WCAG 1.4.4. The style code label no longer goes through useUiCopy. No CMS entry existed for the key, so the lookup already returned its fallback — output is byte-identical, verified by capturing the rendered HTML before and after. useContentful requests entries with no locale parameter, so a CMS-sourced label would have served one space default to all eight storefronts regardless of site. Recipe keys are hoisted to module constants, matching the eight that already exist. Making an unregistered recipe detectable ---------------------------------------- Unregistering a recipe is silent by construction: useStyleConfig returns an empty object, __css={undefined} is a legal prop, and the element inherits. For the two colour-only atoms the inherited value differs from the brand's by one unit per channel, so no visual review would catch it. theme/index.test.tsx's registration list now covers the three new recipes, and the meta molecule additionally asserts its resolved 28px under a ChakraProvider — which catches a wrong value as well as a missing registration, and runs in the unconditional unit-test job rather than the conditional Storybook one. ## The scorer caught a hazard that would have shipped a broken commit

It materialised the git index into `/tmp` and ran the suite against it: **2 files failed, 3 tests failed, 364 tests** — because the index was a revision behind the worktree on 8 files. `theme/index.test.tsx` had never been staged at all.

It also caught that my claim *"I have since replaced intent-to-add with a full `git add`"* was true **only for the one file I'd named** — not for the tree. That's orchestrator error #8, and the most operationally dangerous one yet.

The commit-by-path approach I've been using takes worktree content, so it would likely have been fine — but "likely fine" isn't a gate. Staged everything, re-confirmed 363/24, then committed.

## Its REWORK item was a comment — and it adjudicated a builder correction as *also* wrong

The comment I'd had added claimed the unregistered-atom fallback was Chakra's `gray.900` `#171923`. I verified all three of the scorer's counter-facts myself:

- **SFCC's `gray.900` is `#181818`** — its `foundations/colors.js:39` replaces Chakra's whole scale before our overrides merge
- The `gray.900` reference comes from **SFCC's** `foundations/styles.js:11`, not Chakra
- Our brand `grey.900` is `#191919`

So the real delta is **#181818 vs #191919 — one unit per channel.** Which makes the finding *stronger* than the false version stated: the comment was understating how undetectable an unregistration is, while quoting a hex a reader would search for and never find.

Worth noting the chain: my original claim was wrong, the builder's correction of it was **also** wrong, and the scorer got it right. Three passes on one sentence.

## What COMMIT 3 shipped

7 recipes, 3 new registrations, and four real defects fixed rather than carried — the empty-price node doubling a flex gap, the empty padded box on every page load, both 28px hops from one const, and the CMS label removed with byte-identical output proven by capturing rendered HTML before and after.

Plus the observability fix: unregistering any of the three new recipes now fails a test, verified by the scorer deleting each one individually.

**One gap left open deliberately and recorded in the commit body:** registration is pinned, consumption isn't — `__css={styles}` can be deleted from either colour-only atom with a green suite.

## Next: COMMIT 4, and your second G6

This is the one that puts the Zimmermann layout on the page. It carries the finding the tester surfaced from the cross-commit angle: **delete the `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">` wrapper, don't repopulate it** — keeping it gives 20px + 28px = 48px against a 28px spec, and the molecule's own `play` reads 28px in isolation and passes.

The scorer added a useful detail: `Stack` is still used at `:890` in that file, so removing the wrapper won't create an unused import and G3 stays at 15.

Ready when you are.

- `index.tsx:802` — `<Stack spacing={16}>`.
- Chakra 2.7 `Stack` spaces with `gap`, not a child selector: `node_modules/@chakra-ui/layout/dist/chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs:72,77` — `display: "flex"` / `gap: hasDivider ? void 0 : spacing`. No divider is passed. Token `16` → `4rem` → **64px**.

Measured with a faithful reproduction of the real ancestor chain (`/private/tmp/pdpprobe/src/chain.tsx`, Chromium 1440px):

| measurement | value |
|---|---|
| outer Stack computed | `display: flex`, `flexDirection: column`, `rowGap: 64px` |
| outer Stack direct children | `productview`, `accordion-root`, **`product-meta`**, `recs` |
| **accordions bottom → first meta row** | **92px** (64 gap + 28 paddingTop) |

| meta absent → accordions → recommendations | 64px — identical to base ✓ clean collapse |

*What a reader would do wrong:* trust the comment, believe the recipe owns the hop, and never check the page-level `Stack`. **Fix shape (not applied):** wrapping the meta alone in a `<Box>` does **not** help — the Box just becomes the flex item. The accordion and the meta must share one flex item (e.g. one `<Box>` around both `<InformationAccordion/>` and `<ZimmProductMeta/>`), after which the 28px `paddingTop` is the whole hop.

Sorry — I mixed the design's vocabulary with the code's. Here's the concrete picture.

## What's actually on the page

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:802` opens the main column:

```
<Stack spacing={16}>              ← 64px gap between every child
  <ProductView renderHeader=…/>      the info column: name, price, description
  <InformationAccordion/>            the expandable panels
  <ZimmProductMeta/>                 ← COMMIT 3's molecule: model line + style code
  <RecommendedProducts …/>           the rails
</Stack>
```

`<Island>` wraps some of these but emits **no DOM element** (`partialHydrationEnabled: false`), so all four are direct flex children of that 64px-gap column.

## Why I said "accordions" and the design says "drawers"

Same slot, different names, **and currently different content**:

| | Names |
|---|---|
| **Figma** calls them *drawers* | Details & Care · Size & Fit · Shipping & Returns · Assistance · Label |
| **Base SFCC** component is literally `InformationAccordion` | Product Detail · Size & Fit · Reviews *(Coming Soon)* · Questions *(Coming Soon)* |

Replacing that content is **open item (b)** — which you scoped out of SFCC-89. So base's accordion is what physically occupies the drawers' position today.

When the Figma verification measured *"drawer bottom → model line = 28px"*, that translates in code to *"bottom of `InformationAccordion` → top of `ZimmProductMeta`"*.

## So the defect, in plain terms

**The component is `ZimmProductMeta`** — the model line and style code at the foot of the info column.

The design wants **28px** between the panels above it and the model line. It renders **92px**: the parent Stack contributes 64px, and the molecule's own recipe adds 28px on top.

Two hops were measured in Figma, both at 28px. After COMMIT 4:

| Hop | Design | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| panels → model line | 28px | 84px | **92px** ✗ |
| model line → style code | 28px | 20px | **28px** ✓ |

Neither was ever right. One is now correct; the other moved 8px further away, because deleting the old wrapper removed its 20px padding and the molecule's 28px replaced it — while the parent's 64px was there the whole time and nobody had accounted for it.

**Your a11y answer is recorded** — fix the `aria-live` region now, defer the "From" prefix to SFCC-194 with a PR-body note.

# FIX 1 — the meta block sits 92px below the panels; the design says 28px

**Measured in Chromium by the tester and re-verified by me link by link:**
- `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:802` — `<Stack spacing={16}>`
- Chakra 2.7 `Stack` spaces with `gap`, not a child selector (`@chakra-ui/layout/dist/chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs:72,77` — `display: "flex"`, `gap: hasDivider ? void 0 : spacing`), and no divider is passed
- `space[16]` = `4rem` = **64px**
- `<Island>` emits **no DOM element** — `partialHydrationEnabled: false` in `config/default.js:40`, so `island/index.jsx:88-90` returns `<>{children}</>`

So `ZimmProductMeta`'s root is a **direct flex item** of that 64px-gap column: 64 + its own 28px `paddingTop` = **92px**. It was 84px before this commit (64 + the old wrapper's 20px `paddingTop`) and has never matched the design.

**The developer's ruling: wrap `<InformationAccordion/>` and `<ZimmProductMeta/>` in a single `<Box>`**, so they become one flex child instead of two.

Why this is the right shape and a `<Box>` around the molecule alone is not: a wrapper around only the molecule just becomes the flex item itself and still inherits the 64px. The two must **share** one flex item. Then:
- the `<Box>` inherits the 64px gap above it, so the panels sit exactly where they do today — unchanged
- the panels and the molecule are now siblings inside the Box with no gap between them, so the molecule's 28px `paddingTop` is the **entire** hop
- the recommendations rail below is still the next flex child of the outer Stack, so its 64px gap is unchanged

**Verify all three of those in a probe before reporting** — outside the repo, and reproduce the real ancestor chain (outer Stack → no-op Island → children). Do not assume; the whole reason this defect existed is that nobody checked the parent.

**Path-set expansion, authorised:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` (+ its test). It was committed in COMMIT 3, but the atom only renders on a real page as of COMMIT 4, so the a11y requirement lands here.

- `aria-label` on the price (`:37`, `:49`)
- a `<VisuallyHidden aria-live="polite" aria-atomic={true}>` region (`:57-66`)

content.text:
You've found a real defect. The typography is right; **the colour is wrong**, and the correct token already exists.

## The mismatch

| | Design spec | What we render |
|---|---|---|
| **colour** | `var(--text-secondary, #666)` | `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` → `grey[900]` = **`#191919`** |
| font-family | Futura Round | ✓ `FONT_MEDIUM` |
| font-size | `0.75rem` | ✓ `fontSizes['3xs']` = `0.75rem` |
| font-weight | `500` | ✓ `fontWeights.medium` = `500` |
| line-height | `1.125rem` | ✓ `lineHeights['2xs']` = `1.125rem` |

Four of five match exactly. The colour is off by a lot — **near-black instead of grey.**

## And the token we should have used is already there

- `colour.ts:67` — `secondary: grey[600]`
- `colour.ts:11` — `grey[600] = '#666666'`
- `zimmTokens.ts:49` — `'--zimm-color-text-secondary'`

So `var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)` resolves to **exactly `#666666`** — a precise match for the design's `#666` fallback. The right token existed the whole time and we reached for the wrong one.

## Why nobody caught it

This is the defect the scorer predicted in COMMIT 3, almost word for word. Its exact finding was that the two colour-only recipes are **unobservable** — you can unregister them entirely and every gate stays green, because the fallback differs from the brand value by one unit per channel.

The same blindness applies to using the *wrong* brand token: nothing compares any rendered colour to Figma. `recipeGuards` checks the token is a `var(--zimm-*)` reference, not that it's the *right* one. There is no design-fidelity gate anywhere in this repo.

## The model line has it too

`zimmProductModelInfo.css.ts:23` also uses `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`. In the design both sit in the same meta block, so it's likely wrong the same way — but I only have your spec for the style code, so I'd be guessing.
