# SFCC-89 — closed-loop execution workflow

**Planned 2026-08-26.** Supersedes this file's previous contents (the plan assurance pass, completed
2026-08-25 — its findings are recorded in `sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md`'s five changelogs).

---

## Context

The implementation plan is written, verified, and corrected. What is missing is a way to **execute**
it that does not rest on one agent's discipline holding across 5 commits.

Where we are:

- **The build already exists** — 29 staged files, 3,535 insertions, written 2026-08-24. tsc 0,
  Vitest 354/22, lint at develop's baseline, ACs verified against live SFCC. **Zero commits.**
- **The plan is a re-sequencing plan, not a build plan.** `AGENTS.md`'s copy-first rule requires the
  mechanical TypeScript port to land separately from the functional changes made on top; it got
  bundled (register row D5). With no commits the split is still free. After the first commit lands
  wrong, fixing it means rewriting history on a shared branch.
- **`sfcc-89-realignment-plan.md` is the spec** — 423 lines, 6 steps → 5 commits, per-step gates,
  five changelogs recording 16 verified corrections. **The loop executes it; it does not re-derive it.**
- **Step 0 is done.** Restore point `sfcc-89-wip` @ `3ae8dcd`, byte-exact (tree hash verified three
  times), never pushed. `git checkout sfcc-89-wip -- <path>` restores any single file.

Why a loop rather than just doing it: **Step 1 is a backwards reconstruction across 12 sites where no
gate can detect an omission.** The only mechanical signal is the lint *warning* count sitting at
exactly 15. A single pass that quietly misses three removal sites yields green tsc, green tests, an
unchanged error count, and a wrong commit. Independent verification and scoring is the mitigation.

## The goal, and its five authorities

Build SFCC-89 to spec — not under, not over. "Spec" is five things, and the scorer checks all five:

| # | Authority | Concretely |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The ticket** | Six enumerated fields (name, price, description, model copy, style code, ~~breadcrumb~~); "Contentful-sourced content" excluded; the `c_modelFit` dependency |
| 2 | **Figma** | `pdp/product-content` Desktop `40000307:14062` / Mobile `40000343:9727`; measured values only, frames/instances not TEXT nodes, no cross-file comparison |
| 3 | **The docs** | `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/*` — copy-first, minimal changes, tier rules, no new packages |
| 4 | **PR #59, now in develop** | The established precedent and this branch's base: camelCase `ui-kits/`, co-located `<name>.css.ts`, `var(--zimm-*)` in recipes not JSX, registered in `theme/components/index.ts` |
| 5 | **Token / component / CSS / override structure** | `textStyle` for type · `var(--zimm-*)` for colour+spacing · recipe per component · relative imports for already-overridden components · faithful default export on shared bridges |

## Role mapping — with one honest adjustment

**No custom agents exist in this repo or at user level** (`.claude/agents/` is absent in both). All
five roles are greenfield.

| Requested role | Implemented as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator + scope checker** | **The session (me)** | Only the session can dispatch subagents, hold state across iterations, run gates, and own the commit boundary. Already holds the plan, register and Jira context. |
| **Builder / implementer** | Fresh subagent per commit | Gets the step verbatim + the constraint set. Fresh, not a fork — so it cannot inherit my assumptions about what "done" looks like. |
| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Re-runs no gate I already ran; dispatches angle-specific sub-checks and consolidates. Keeps raw output out of my context. |
| **Scorer** | Fresh subagent, independent of builder | Gets diff + gate numbers + tester report + CodeRabbit findings + the 5-authority rubric. Returns PASS or REWORK with cited defects. |
| **Retrospective / meta** | Subagent at each boundary, fed a structured log | **The adjustment:** it cannot "listen while the loop runs" — subagents cannot observe each other's traffic, and only the session sees everything. So it is invoked at each boundary with an iteration log, and its output edits the *next* iteration's briefs. Same effect, one boundary of latency. |

Amendments persist to `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/loop-briefs.md` so improvements accumulate across all 5
commits instead of being re-learned.

## Carry-forwards from COMMIT 1 — assigned by which commit owns the file

Commit-by-path discipline means a fix belongs to the commit that already opens its file.

- **COMMIT 2** (`product-view/index.tsx`): delete the three inert `cloneElement` casts at `:594-596`
  **and** the 7-line comment at `:585-591` that exists only to explain them — proven inert by deletion
  (tsc clean, lint unchanged). Also fix `ProductViewRefScope`'s JSDoc at **`:169-170`** (*"React's own `Ref<T>` type cannot express a `this`-bound callback, so consumers assert against this type at the prop site"*) — the same claim disproved at `product-detail`. It is written as
  guidance, so it propagates.
- **COMMIT 4** (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx`): delete the inert `} as unknown as React.Ref<HTMLDivElement>`
  at `:756`. Verified the only remaining candidate in that file — `:257`/`:648` are SDK-param casts and
  `:281`/`:290`/`:492` are the three error-narrowing casts the developer ruled to leave.
- **COMMIT 4** (G5): read the **acknowledged** list, not just the unacknowledged count. Expect 21.

## Reuse, don't rebuild

Three existing skills cover parts of this. Their call sites differ and matter:

- **`/scope-check`** — a **pre-flight prompt linter**, not a diff auditor. Reads the tier rules and
  predicts what a prompt would touch, returning SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED and rewriting the prompt when
  needed. Correct call site: orchestrator, **before** dispatching each builder. Caveat: `BLOCKED`
  means "stop and get owner approval" — a deliberate human gate.
- **`/code-quality`** — a **post-hoc convention auditor** that already fans out to 4 parallel agents
  and emits a numeric `🔴 must-fix` count, a ready-made pass signal for the scorer. Two caveats: it
  **defaults its baseline to `main`** (we need `develop` — pin it explicitly), and it audits
  conventions, not behaviour, so the tester still owns the gates.
- **`/code-review`** (CodeRabbit CLI) — **mandated, not optional.** `AGENTS.md`'s Coding Task
  Workflow step 4: *"Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review…
  The CLI is required, not optional."* Verified available: **v0.7.5, authenticated, org
  ZimmermannAU, Pro, seat assigned.** Supports `--agent` (structured findings for agent workflows),
  `--light`, `--base`. This becomes **G7** below.

## The loop, per commit

```
  ORCHESTRATOR  pre-flight: restate the step's deliverables from the plan; confirm
                branch/HEAD/state; /scope-check the builder prompt before dispatch
        │
        ▼
  BUILDER       implement that step only → report changed files + rationale
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  run the deterministic gates myself (G1/G2/G3/G5) → capture real numbers
        │
        ▼
  TESTER        fan out to angle agents → consolidated findings (no gate re-runs)
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  G4 (Storybook) + G7 (CodeRabbit --agent) → structured findings
        │
        ▼
  SCORER        diff + gates + tester + CodeRabbit vs the 5-authority rubric
        │
        ├── REWORK ──► BUILDER (cited defects) ──► gates ──► TESTER ──► SCORER   [max 3]
        │                                                        │
        │                                          3rd REWORK ──► ESCALATE
        ▼
       PASS
        │
        ▼
  ORCHESTRATOR  scope re-check (under- AND over-delivery) → commit → G6 hard stop if due
        │
        ▼
  RETROSPECTIVE structured log → concrete brief edits → applied to the next commit
```

## Agent briefs

**Builder** (fresh, per commit) — gets the step verbatim; the 5-authority constraint set; the gate
numbers it must leave behind; the restore command; an explicit *do-not* list (no commits, no package
installs, no Tier 1 files, no `npm start`, no test-config edits, **never append args to
`npm run lint`**). Returns changed files with a one-line rationale each, plus anything it could not
do and why. **Never commits.**

**Tester** (per iteration) — gets the diff, the step's acceptance criteria, and the gate numbers
already measured. Fans out to four angles: (a) rules/tier compliance, (b) design-token and recipe
fidelity, (c) test/story coverage of this step's own contract, (d) base-parity regression — did
anything the plan did not name change? Returns findings with `file:line`, each CONFIRMED or
PLAUSIBLE, and **a mandatory "what I could not verify" section** — D17 survived eight invocations
because every pass reported only what it had checked.

**Scorer** (fresh, independent) — gets diff, gate numbers, tester report, CodeRabbit findings, the
step's plan text, the rubric. Returns per-axis PASS/REWORK with cited defects. Overall PASS only if
every axis passes **and** every gate number matches the plan exactly. **Must state what it tried to
falsify** — a PASS with no falsification attempt is not a PASS.

**Retrospective** (per boundary) — gets the iteration log: rework rounds, what the scorer caught,
what the tester missed that the scorer found (or vice versa), any gate surprise. Returns concrete
brief edits ("builder brief: add X to the do-not list"), not sentiments.

## The five commits

| | Subject | Steps | G6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `refactor(product-view): copy-first TypeScript port of product-view and product-detail` | 1 + 2 (+ `routes.tsx`, `vendor.d.ts`) | **hard stop** |
| 2 | `feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content` | 3 | — |
| 3 | `feat(ui-kits): add PDP static product information atoms and molecules` | 4a–4f | — |
| 4 | `feat(pdp): render static product information on the product detail page` | 5 | **hard stop** |
| 5 | `refactor(pdp): extract the static product header into a testable partial` | 6 | — |

## Gates — orchestrator-run, per commit

All 29 files stay on disk throughout; each commit selects contents **by path**. Timings measured on
this machine.

| | Command | Time | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 15s | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| G2 | `npx vitest run` | 15s | 354/22 | 354/22 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 | ≥355/24 |
| G3 | `npm run lint` | 15s | 17 / **16 warn** | 17/**16** | 17/15 | 17/15 | 17/15 |
| G4 | Storybook interaction + a11y | **8s** (static) | 100/22 | 100/22 | 102/23 | 102/23 | 105/24 |
| G5 | `npm run audit:tokens` | 0.4s | 19→**14** | 14 | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| G7 | `cr review --light --agent --base develop` | ~1-3 min | required | required | required | required | required |
| G6 | Developer, live PDP | — | **stop** | — | — | **stop** | — |

**G3 is load-bearing at COMMIT 1** — the only signal that can catch a missed Step 1 removal.
**Corrected during execution — measured 16 at COMMIT 1, not 15.** Under the constant-tree rule all 29 files are on disk, so `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx:33`'s `_key` counts at C1–C2; it goes at C3 when 4e deletes that test. Baseline **16 at C1–C2 (ceiling 26), 15 from C3**. Error count is a 17 invariant throughout. What actually matters is **zero `no-unused-vars` in the files the step edits** — the headline total is a proxy.

**Inner loop (~45s, offline, zero repo writes)** — G1 → scoped G2 → G3 → G5. A scoped Vitest run is
**8× faster**: `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-detail` is 1.8s vs 15s. Full G2 before
every commit, always.

**G4 needs neither `http-server` nor `build-storybook`.** The CI recipe uses `npx http-server
storybook-static`, and `http-server` is genuinely absent from `package.json`, `node_modules`, and
global. But `test-storybook`'s default `--url` is already `http://127.0.0.1:6006` — exactly what
`npm run storybook` serves:

```
python3 -m http.server 6007 --directory storybook-static &   # any free port
npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6007 --timeout 30000
node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6007
```
**Measured 8.07s / 7.66s, not the ~2 min estimated.** The `storybook dev` recipe previously written
here is the *slow* path and touches a developer-owned process; this one does neither.

**Precondition — this shortcut is CONDITIONAL, not general.** Reusing an existing `storybook-static`
is valid only when the diff touches nothing in a story's import graph:
`grep -rln "<changed-path>" --include="*.stories.tsx" overrides/` must return **nothing**. That held at
COMMIT 1 and holds at COMMIT 2. **It is VOID at COMMIT 3 and COMMIT 5** — both rewrite files inside the
story graph, so `test-storybook` against a stale build would render the *old* components and report a
green count while exercising nothing new. **Rebuild there.**

Nothing written to `storybook-static/`, and incremental rebuilds between iterations instead of a
2-4 min cold build each time. `test-storybook`, `wait-on` and **Playwright's chromium
(`chromium-1223`) are all present** — verified, so no network needed. It is a long-lived background
process the loop must own and reap. Zero-dependency fallback: `python3 -m http.server 6006
--directory storybook-static`.

**G4 is more aggressive than it looks.** `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets `a11y: { test: 'error' }`, so
**all 100 stories are a11y assertions**, not just the 37 carrying a `play`.

**Playwright is out of the loop entirely.** No PDP spec exists — `e2e/tests/` holds one file (two
homepage smoke tests). `ProductPage.js` scaffolding exists unused, there is no `e2e_pdp` allow-list
group, and change-scoping for our diff falls back to the full suite (those same two tests). Writing
one is blocked by a hard human gate: the Gherkin-first workflow requires Lead QA sign-off *before*
any Playwright code. Not a gap this loop can close.

**Two gates the loop is the sole enforcement for.** Neither `tsc --noEmit` nor `audit:tokens` is
wired into any CI workflow — `qa.yml` has no typecheck job. G1 and G5 are not extra diligence; they
are the only place those checks happen before merge.

## Loop hazards — hard-code these as guardrails

Five ways an automated loop silently corrupts its own signal here. All verified in source.

1. **`npm run lint` can be turned into a writer.** `package.json` has
   `"lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix"`, and `pwa-kit-dev lint` forwards `--`-args verbatim into a
   shell `execSync`. Plain `npm run lint` is confirmed non-mutating, but **any appended argument**
   changes that. Pin the literal string, no interpolation. `lint:fix` and `pwa-kit-dev format` are
   **forbidden** in the verify phase — auto-formatting would erase the very prettier errors that
   make the 17-error count an invariant.
2. **`vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true`.** A typo'd path filter exits **0** having run
   nothing. **Assert on the reported test count, never the exit code.**
3. **G3 and G5 exit non-zero at a healthy baseline** — lint exits 1 with its 17 pre-existing
   prettier errors, `audit:tokens` exits 1 with its 19. **Diff the counts; ignore the exit code.**
   Two pre-existing `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` stderr lines from `theme/index.test.tsx` are
   noise on a *passing* suite — stderr is not failure.
4. **`PostToolUse` hooks mutate what the builder wrote.** `Write` triggers `prettier --write` on the
   new file; `Edit|Write` triggers `registryUpdate.sh` → `generateRegistry.mjs --file=<path>`, which
   rewrites `.claude/registry/*.md` **on every single edit**. So registry churn appears in
   `git status` continuously, not just at commit time. The scorer must expect and ignore both.
5. **`.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` is a `Stop` hook that blocks on a dirty tree.** Verified: it
   returns `{"decision":"block"}` whenever `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, on any branch,
   instructing Claude to write a proposal to `.docs/agents-proposals/` and *"end the session — do
   not start new work."* It has a `stop_hook_active` re-entry guard. Our tree is never clean during
   the loop, so it fires at every turn boundary.

   **This is why the loop is orchestrator-driven and does not use the `ralph-loop` plugin.**
   `ralph-loop` drives iteration via its *own* `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` — two
   blocking Stop hooks racing on one turn with contradictory instructions. Fixing that would mean
   editing `.claude/settings.json`, which is **Tier 1**. Dispatching subagents from within a single
   orchestrator turn per commit sidesteps it entirely: the Stop hook then fires only at commit
   boundaries, where a pause is wanted anyway.

## Decisions settled by the developer, 2026-08-26

1. **All 5 commits pre-authorised** — the loop commits at each boundary, but *only* after the scorer
   returns PASS and the scope re-check clears. The five subjects above are the authorisation of
   record; anything else needs a fresh ask. Note `git add`/`commit`/`push` are not in either
   permissions allowlist, so commits may prompt — the scratch-branch commit did succeed earlier, so
   this is a verify-at-runtime item, not a blocker.
2. **Hard stop at both G6 points** — after COMMIT 1 and COMMIT 4. COMMIT 1's G6 proves the
   TypeScript override renders at all; everything after it assumes that.
3. **3 rework rounds per commit**, then escalate rather than loop again.
4. **Over-delivery is flagged, not auto-reverted** — anything beyond the plan's enumerated
   deliverables is reported with the diff, and the scorer withholds PASS until the developer rules.

## Termination and escalation

The loop stops — not retries — on any of:
- 3 rework rounds on one commit
- A gate number the plan does not predict that the scorer cannot explain
- Any Tier 1 path, `package.json`, or test-config file appearing in a diff
- `/scope-check` returning BLOCKED
- Scope divergence needing a developer ruling
- Either G6 hard stop
- `pre-commit` failing for a reason unrelated to the change (it has four independent `exit 1` paths)

## Verification — how we know the loop itself worked

1. `git diff sfcc-89-wip -- <the 29 paths>` shows **only** the plan's enumerated deltas.
2. Every commit's gate numbers match the table above, recorded per commit.
3. Every scorer PASS cites what it tried to falsify.
4. Every tester "could not verify" section is non-empty or explicitly reasoned empty.
5. `loop-briefs.md` shows at least one concrete brief amendment — a retrospective that changed
   nothing across 5 commits did not observe anything.
6. G7 ran on every commit, per `AGENTS.md`'s requirement, with each finding either fixed or
   explicitly dispositioned.

## What this does not do

- It does not re-plan. The realignment plan is the spec; disagreeing with its **scope** escalates, not
  forks. **Narrow carve-out, added after COMMIT 1:** a role may decline a specific *instruction* when
  following it would make a file's own documentation false, or would reproduce the defect the step
  exists to fix — provided it reports `REFUSED: <instruction> — <why> — <what I did instead>`. This
  happened at COMMIT 1 and the refusal was correct; the scorer independently confirmed it beat the
  instruction. The orchestrator's instruction is not more authoritative than the file's observable state.
- **Scorer input package format is mandatory:** every attribution is marked `MEASURED: <n> (<exact
  command>)` or `CLAIMED: <assertion> (source: builder|tester)`. The scorer may not treat CLAIMED as
  established. A COMMIT 1 error lived entirely inside this artefact.
- It does not push, open a PR, or write the PR body. The breadcrumb note is deferred and there is
  nothing to write it against yet.
- It does not resolve the four open items — `c_modelFit` (owner Dani, two-step), breadcrumb ACs
  (developer), open item (b) (scoped out), (d) SFCC-723, (e) PRC-12.
- It does not add PDP E2E coverage — human-gated, see Gates.
- It does not guarantee nothing is missed. D17 survived eight invocations of a comparable loop.

*                     Zimmermann `2xs` (0.875rem / 14px) was intended. Plausible, wrong size.
 *   fontSize: '4xs' → no Chakra key, so `font-size: 4xs` is emitted and the browser drops the
 *                     declaration outright. Same for every `lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` key,
 *                     none of which collide with a Chakra default.
 *   fontSize: 'l'   → a spacing key that is not a fontSizes key: dropped the same way.
 *
 * `fontSizes` is the only one of the three with genuine wrong-value collisions; the other two
 * only ever drop the declaration. Both outcomes are worth guarding.
 *
 * Set type with `textStyle` (all 22 Handover styles ARE registered) or var(--zimm-font-*).
 * `fontWeight` is deliberately absent: `medium` is a key in both scales and resolves to 500
 * either way, so keying it the same way would flag a correct declaration.
 */
const TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS = new Map<string, Set<string>>([
  ['fontSize', new Set([...Object.keys(fontSizes), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
  ['lineHeight', new Set([...Object.keys(lineHeights), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
  ['letterSpacing', new Set([...Object.keys(letterSpacings), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
]);

/** Properties that resolve through `theme.space`, where a bare scale key is correct. */
const SPACE_SHORTHANDS = new Set(['padding', 'margin', 'inset', 'gap', 'p', 'm']);

/** Derived from the registered breakpoints so the two cannot drift apart. */
const BREAKPOINT_KEYS = new Set(Object.keys(breakpoints));

/**
 * True when `n` is a responsive *value* container — an array (`['xl','2xl']`) or a
 * breakpoint-keyed object (`{base:'xl', md:'2xl'}`) — rather than a style object. Its keys are
 * therefore positions, not property names, and the property name has to come from the parent.
 *
 * The test is deliberately "are ALL the keys breakpoints?" and not "is ANY key a breakpoint?".

 * only ever drop the declaration. Both outcomes are worth guarding.

 * `fontWeight` is deliberately absent: `medium` is a key in both scales and resolves to 500
 * either way, so keying it the same way would flag a correct declaration.
 */
const TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS = new Map<string, Set<string>>([
  ['fontSize', new Set([...Object.keys(fontSizes), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
  ['lineHeight', new Set([...Object.keys(lineHeights), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
  ['letterSpacing', new Set([...Object.keys(letterSpacings), ...SPACING_KEYS])],
]);

/** Properties that resolve through `theme.space`, where a bare scale key is correct. */
const SPACE_SHORTHANDS = new Set(['padding', 'margin', 'inset', 'gap', 'p', 'm']);

/** Derived from the registered breakpoints so the two cannot drift apart. */
const BREAKPOINT_KEYS = new Set(Object.keys(breakpoints));

/**

 * therefore positions, not property names, and the property name has to come from the parent.

```
BASE ONLY    -> {"declared":{...},"undeclared":{"color":"blue"}}   ← baseStyle NOT gated

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts:209-210` — "`textStyle` is a special key Chakra's style engine expands wherever it appears"
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/zimmNavItem.css.ts:14-16` — "textStyle is expanded in place by Chakra's style engine"

Sites (line numbers are from the current working tree; verify before editing):
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/zimmProductPrice.css.ts:14-20` — "would therefore have been silently overwritten by the element's prop"
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/zimmProductName.css.ts:15-20` — see R2 too, same block
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductModelInfo/zimmProductModelInfo.css.ts:14-17` — "an element prop out-ranks a recipe"
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductDescription/zimmProductDescription.css.ts` — around line 59, "out-ranks everything a recipe resolves"
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:16-20` — "would out-rank everything this recipe resolves"
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:25-26` — "or SFCC-194's `sale` variant cannot override it". This one is *nearly* right under the corrected rule; make it precise about which kind of override it means.

## R2 — a claim of guard coverage that does not exist

`zimmProductName.css.ts:15` opens "Type is set here too, **for the same reason the colour is**", which read against `:11-13` ("`recipeGuards.test.ts` can only mechanically catch the mistake inside a registered recipe … Moving the value here puts it under that guard") asserts that `textStyle` is now covered by that guard. It is not. MEASURED: `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:153-157`'s `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` map checks exactly `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing` — and its docblock at ~`:149` names `textStyle` as the *recommended remedy*, not a checked prop. A typo'd `textStyle: 'heading33'` in a recipe is caught by nothing: not `tsc`, not the guard, not axe.

`:9-13` is **true about the colour** and stays. Sever the false extension to type, and say plainly that `textStyle` is not guarded either way (this is not a regression — a typo'd JSX prop was equally unguarded — but the added coverage must not be claimed).

## R3 — three missing registration pins

`overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx`'s `component overrides are registered` test pins only 4 of the 7 registered `ZimmProduct*` recipes. Add the missing three:
- `ZimmProductDescription`, `ZimmProductStyleCode`, `ZimmProductContent`

All seven are registered — verified at `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:13-19` (imports) and `:34-40` (registration). Follow the existing `expect(theme.components.X).toBeTruthy();` form.

**The surrounding comment's arithmetic must be corrected too.** It currently says "these **four** fail silently" and "For the **three atoms** each `baseStyle` is exactly `margin: 0`, one colour and a `textStyle`". With seven pinned, "four" is wrong, and Description/StyleCode/Content do **not** fit that `margin: 0` + colour + `textStyle` description — Description carries descendant rules and a list indent, StyleCode is multipart with a flex row, Content is the molecule's flex column. Rewrite so the comment describes what is actually pinned. Read each of the three recipes before characterising it; do not guess.

Also worth stating in that comment, because it is the reason two of these three matter more than they used to: the same batch moved type off the JSX element and into these recipes, so an unregistration now additionally costs all type, not just colour and spacing.

## R4 — `recipeParts.test.ts`'s stated failure mode is false

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:5-7` currently says: *"Chakra returns a styles object keyed by the recipe's `parts`; reading a key that is not declared yields `undefined`, and `__css={undefined}` is a perfectly legal prop. The element renders unstyled…"*

**`parts` does not gate `baseStyle`.** MEASURED by direct probe against the real `ChakraProvider` — a recipe declaring `parts: ['declared']` but carrying `baseStyle: {declared, undeclared}` and `variants: {v: {declared, undeclared}}` resolved as:
```
baseStyle only    -> {"declared":{"color":"red"},"undeclared":{"color":"blue"}}
baseStyle+variant -> {"declared":{"color":"red","margin":"1px"},"undeclared":{"color":"blue"}}
```
So the undeclared part **keeps its full baseStyle** and **silently loses the variant's styles**. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`, not `baseStyle`. Corroborating live evidence in-repo: the base SFCC recipe at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/project/header.js` declares **no `parts` key at all**, and every one of its `baseStyle` keys resolves and is used.

Correct the stated mechanism. Note that this makes the guard's justification **stronger**, not weaker, and say so: the real silent failure is a part that renders with its base styling and then quietly stops responding to variants and sizes — which is *latent* on a recipe that has no variants today and appears only the day someone adds one. That is precisely the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case `.claude/rules/testing.md` says to cover.

**Do not change the guard's logic or scope.** Its check (reads-missing-from-`parts`) and its walk root stay exactly as they are. The paragraph at `:9-13` explaining why comparing `parts` against `baseStyle` keys would not catch a co-renamed part is still true and stays. Only the failure-mode description at `:5-7` is wrong.

# One thing that is NOT yours to fix

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 1 literally prescribes the JSX-prop form (`textStyle="body2"`), which this batch moves away from. That file is **Tier 1 governance** and the conflict is the developer's call — it is being escalated separately. Do not edit it, and do not add a comment asserting the doc endorses the recipe form. `zimmProductName.css.ts:22` currently cites hierarchy point 1 as endorsing what the code does; soften that to what is defensible — the doc names `textStyle` as the correct way to set type (true, and the reason it stays a bare key rather than a `var(--zimm-*)`), without claiming it blesses the recipe-vs-prop placement. For context you may use but must not cite as a rules file: as of `develop`, PR #59 put `textStyle` inside **seven** recipe files and on **zero** JSX props in any non-story component, so the recipe form is the established precedent in this codebase.

# Verify before you report

Run, in order, and report the actual numbers:
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` → expect 0
2. `npx vitest run` → expect **370 passed / 25 files**
3. `npm run lint` → expect **17 errors / 15 warnings**
4. `npm run audit:tokens` → expect **14 unacknowledged / 22 acknowledged**

Then prove R3 is not vacuous: temporarily remove one of the three newly-pinned recipes from `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`'s registration object, re-run only `npx vitest run overrides/app/theme`, confirm the new assertion **fails**, and restore. Report the failure message you saw. A pin that cannot fail is not a pin.

# Report format

For each of R1–R4: the files touched, and one line on what the corrected claim now says. Then the four gate numbers as measured, and the R3 falsification result. Then a section headed **"What I could not verify"** — mandatory, and if genuinely empty, say why. Finally, if you declined any instruction above because following it would have made a file's documentation false or reproduced the defect it exists to fix, report it as `REFUSED: <instruction> — <why> — <what I did instead>`. That carve-out is legitimate and has been exercised correctly twice in this project; the orchestrator's instruction is not more authoritative than a file's observable state.

TITLE: feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI — shell, layout, and ui-kit component structure

# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke
- `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — colour derivation moved out of the hook into the
  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — prop extraction scoped to `<ComponentName>Props`,
  Markdown table cells escaped, comma-containing types no longer silently dropped

# How to test-drive this PR

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → `/`, scroll to the footer. Nav columns hug their
  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it
- Resize through **1030px → 760px** — the bottom bar stays aligned with the content above
  it at every width
- Type a valid email → `>` opens the Join Us modal; empty or malformed is blocked inline
  with no modal
- `npm run storybook` → `Layout/Footer` (4 states incl. modal-open), `Elements/ZimmNavItem`
  (unsafe-href fallback), `Forms/ZimmInputAction` (validation)

# Protection-tier check

> ⚠️ **Tier 1** — `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` (test config, **Integration-owned**)
> for serving and mounting the self-hosted fonts; `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`
> (governance, **both squad leads + Integration lead**) to record them;
> `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` (design system, **UI-Designer-owned**) — whitespace only,
> and it now diffs to **zero** against `develop`.
> Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `components/footer/`, `components/header/` (comments only),
> `theme/components/` (**UI-Designer — notified**). `components/footer/` is Global Shell,
> owned by **both squads** — Squad A notified.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `header` unused-import warnings, documented in-file)
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 168/168
- [x] Storybook interaction — 15 `play` functions across 7 stories
- [x] Runtime behaviour — 20/20 (hover, focus-visible, validation, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index above the sticky header)
- [x] Figma geometry — structural paddings exact at 64/48, 48/48, 24/24
- [x] Box model — 112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings/margins/gaps/borders
- [x] Accessibility — axe 0 violations / 17 passes (wcag2a → 2.2aa)
- [x] Local CodeRabbit — no new findings

TITLE: feat(pdp): SFCC-89 static product information — name, price, description, model line, and style code

# Description

Renders the five static product fields on the PDP per SFCC-89 — product name, full
price in the active storefront's currency, description, "Model is…" copy, and style
code — as five ui-kit atoms composed by two molecules, consumed by the product detail
page. No commerce interaction, no Contentful, no gallery: swatches (SFCC-91), size and
add-to-bag (SFCC-92), the gallery (SFCC-186/187/188), accordions (SFCC-195/102), badges
(SFCC-132/225) and was/now pricing (SFCC-194) are all separate stories and none of them
is touched here.

The model line reads `c_modelFit`. Nothing scrapes `c_sizeFit`.

Seven points worth surfacing before review:

- **The copy-first port is its own commit and reviewable on its own.** `d1fb034` is the
  mechanical `.jsx` → `.tsx` port of `product-view` and `product-detail` with **zero**
  functional change — `AGENTS.md`'s copy-first rule requires that split, and it is the
  largest commit by line count. Reading it first makes the other five small.
- **`product-view/index.tsx` gains exactly one optional slot, `renderHeader`.** The
  default export stays a faithful, undecorated SFCC bridge — base components import this
  module, so its prop surface and `forwardRef` behaviour are unchanged and the slot
  defaults to the base header. No other slots were added speculatively.
- **Type sits in the recipes, not on the JSX elements — and this conflicts with a rule
  file.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 1 gives `textStyle="body2"`
  (a prop) as the prescribed form. As of `develop`, PR #59 put `textStyle` inside **seven**
  recipe files and on **zero** JSX props in any non-story component, so the recipe form is
  the established practice and the doc's example is the stale surface. **This needs a
  ruling** — either `overrideStyling.md` point 1 gets updated or this placement is recorded
  as a deliberate override. Flagged rather than resolved: that file is Tier 1 governance.
- **Five changed files have no CODEOWNERS rule, so GitHub auto-requests no reviewer for
  them.** There is no default (`*`) owner in CODEOWNERS. Named by hand below.
- **The loading state diverges from base deliberately.** Base renders nothing until the
  product resolves; this page wraps the static fields in a `Skeleton` with a
  `minHeight` pinned to a line-height token, so the info column does not reflow when the
  data lands. Called out because it is a visible behavioural difference from the base PDP.
- **`formatPrice` is duplicated** between the page and `partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`.
  The partial carries a comment pointing at the page's copy and vice versa. Left duplicated
  rather than lifted to `utils/` — extracting it would be refactoring upward out of this
  story's scope. Worth a follow-up.
- **N of the commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `PostToolUse` hook regenerates
  it on any `components/`/`pages/` edit and the `pre-commit` hook `git add`s it. Mechanical
  — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx:299` spreads `{...styles.popoverContent}` off a recipe that declares no
such part, in both our override and the base template it was copied from
(`retail-react-app/app/components/header/index.jsx:265`) — `popoverContent` is a **ListMenu**
part, so it is an upstream cross-recipe name mixup. It resolves to `undefined` and
`{...undefined}` is a legal no-op, so nothing breaks and Chakra's own `Popover` recipe styles
the element anyway. Pre-existing, out of scope here, and the only instance repo-wide; it
surfaces in the changed-files view because this PR ports that file. Worth its own ticket.

# Linked

> lists the same path as Squad A territory. CODEOWNERS is the enforced surface, so Squad B
> is auto-requested. Both squads ticked so neither is surprised.

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/product-view/index.tsx` — copy-first TS port, plus one optional
  `renderHeader` slot. Default export unchanged in shape
- `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — copy-first TS port, then composes the static fields;
  no container mirroring `pdp/product-content` was introduced, the page composes directly
- `pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — the SFCC → view-model mapper (`c_modelFit`,
  `longDescription`, style code, price), with its own unit suite
- `pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx` — the header assembly, extracted
  so it is testable without the page
- `components/ui-kits/atoms/` — `zimmProductName`, `zimmProductPrice`,
  `zimmProductDescription`, `zimmProductModelInfo`, `zimmProductStyleCode`
- `components/ui-kits/molecules/` — `zimmProductContent` (the text group's rhythm),
  `zimmProductMeta` (model line + style code)
- `components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` — guard widened from `ui-kits/**` to
  `components/**`, newly covering the three footer recipes. `theme/components/header.ts`
  remains deliberately unguarded (not co-located) and says so in-file
- `utils/richText.tsx` — the description's rich-text parser, with its own suite
- `theme/components/index.ts` — registers the seven new recipes
- `theme/index.test.tsx` — registration pins; `useStyleConfig` returns `{}` for an
  unregistered recipe and `__css={undefined}` is legal, so an unregistration is otherwise
  silent
- `routes.tsx`, `types/vendor.d.ts` — route wiring and the vendor type surface the port needs

# Reviewers to name by hand

No CODEOWNERS rule matches these, and there is no default owner:

- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — shared SFCC bridge, imported by base

- `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx` — registration pins
- `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` + `richText.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`

# How to test-drive this PR

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → any PDP. Name, price, description, model line and
  style code render in the info column; switching a variant updates the price
- Switch a variant with a screen reader on — the price is announced without focus moving
  (WCAG 2.2 AA 4.1.3). It is a live region on the price element itself, not a duplicate node
- Resize through the mobile breakpoint — the info column keeps its 64/28/28/64 rhythm
- `npm run storybook` → `Commerce/` for the five atoms and two molecules, `Pages/PDP`
  for the header partial

# Protection-tier check

> **No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR.**
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (Global Shell, **both squads**; CODEOWNERS
> additionally routes it to tier-1 and tier-2 approvers, so their review is auto-requested)
> and `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (**UI-Designer-owned** — registration
> entries only, no design values). `overrides/app/components/product-view/` is treated as
> Tier 2 by convention; note no tier list or CODEOWNERS entry actually covers it.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Not wired into CI; this is the only place it runs
- [x] `npm run lint` — 17 errors / 15 warnings, both at `develop`'s baseline. Error count
      held as an invariant across all commits
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 370 passed / 25 files
- [x] Storybook interaction + a11y — 24 suites / 106 tests. `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets
      `a11y: {test: 'error'}`, so every story is also an axe assertion
- [x] `npm run audit:tokens` — 14 unacknowledged / 22 acknowledged, unchanged from
      `develop`. Not wired into CI either
- [x] Local CodeRabbit (`cr review --light --base develop`) — no findings
- [x] Runtime behaviour on a live PDP — developer-verified at two checkpoints
- **N/A: Playwright.** No PDP spec exists (`e2e/tests/` holds two homepage smoke tests) and
      writing one is gated on Lead QA signing off a Gherkin `.feature` first, per the
      three-stage workflow. Not closable in this PR
BODY

content.text:
Rework complete and verified. One thing changed materially along the way. ## G7 caught a real bug — not a style nit `utils/richText.tsx` unwound its tag stack with `findIndex`, which scans from the **root**, so a closing tag matched its *outermost* same-named frame and closed that frame's ancestors with it: ``` IN :
  • a
    • b
    c
OUT:
  • a
    • b
c ← "c" escaped the list entirely ``` Nested lists and nested emphasis are both authorable in Business Manager, so this would have shipped displaced description copy. Fixed with an innermost-first search (`findLastIndex` needs lib ES2023; the project pins ES2019 and `tsconfig.json` is Tier 1), plus **4 regression tests — each confirmed to fail with the bug restored and pass with the fix.** ## The four corrections | | What was false | Now | |---|---|---| | R1 | 5 recipes + `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` claimed a JSX `textStyle` out-ranks recipe font props | States the measured rule: it doesn't (the composite yields), but it *does* displace a recipe's own `textStyle` — which is what the move actually protects | | R2 | `zimmProductName.css.ts` implied `textStyle` gained guard coverage | Says plainly it gains none, and isn't a regression either | | R3 | Only 4 of 7 recipes pinned | All 7, with the comment's arithmetic corrected against each recipe | | R4 | `recipeParts.test.ts` said `parts` gates `baseStyle` | Says it gates `variants`/`sizes`, and why that makes the guard *more* justified | The builder refused one of my instructions and was right to: I'd told it the base SFCC header recipe "declares no `parts` key at all" — it declares 9, and my claim came from a truncated 60-line read. It shipped the stronger accurate version instead (9 parts vs 13 `baseStyle` keys, the 4 omitted ones read at lines 232/255/321/323). I verified that independently and fixed a transposed name-to-line pairing in it. ## All seven gates, measured by me **G1 0 · G2 374/25 · G3 17err/15warn · G4 24 suites/106 · G5 14/22 · G7 no new findings** 19 files staged, +360/−56. Total against `develop` if committed: **43 files, +4,589/−6.** HEAD unmoved at `3920caf`. ## Why I've stopped here Your pre-authorisation covered five named commit subjects. All five are landed. This would be a seventh commit, and the plan's own terms say anything beyond those five needs a fresh ask — so I'm not committing without it. The work is staged and gated; nothing is lost by waiting. Separately, one ruling is yours, not mine: `overrideStyling.md` point 1 prescribes `textStyle="body2"` as a prop, while #59 put it in seven recipes and zero props. The code follows #59. That file is Tier 1, so I've flagged it in the PR body rather than editing it.

fix(pdp): consolidate the static product info styling surface and close its test gaps

Six pre-PR fixes from three audit passes (design fidelity, local rules, PR #59
conformance), plus four documentation corrections raised by the scorer.

- Style-code label goes through `intl.formatMessage` under
  `product_view.label.style_code`, matching the base template's sibling ids. No
  `translations/` entry is added: react-intl falls back to `defaultMessage`, and each
  site's default locale is silent because `config/sites.js` sets `defaultLocale` to its
  first locale. Non-default locales emit one warning per render until extraction runs.
- Type moves off the JSX elements and into all five recipes, matching #59's practice
  (seven recipes, zero JSX props on `develop`). Measured output-equivalent: three of the
  five are byte-identical including the emotion hash; `zimmProductDescription` and
  `zimmProductStyleCode` change only their hash, with identical declarations and
  identical computed style.
- `recipeParts.test.ts`'s walk root widens from `ui-kits/**` to `components/**`, newly
  covering the three footer recipes. `theme/components/header.ts` stays out of reach by
  design — the model is sibling-based and that recipe is not co-located.
- `ZimmProductName` renders nothing without a name, the same contract as the price and
  description atoms, so a caller can place it unconditionally.
- All seven `ZimmProduct*` recipes are now pinned in `theme/index.test.tsx`, not four.
  An unregistration is otherwise silent: `useStyleConfig` returns `{}` and
  `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop.
- `staticProductHeader` gains a bundle-member story, the branch that suppresses the price.

Four claims in shipped comments were measurably wrong and are corrected:

- Five recipes and `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` said a JSX `textStyle` out-ranks
  individual font properties in a recipe. It does not — `getWithPriority` expands a
  composite by skipping any property already present in the merged object, so the
  expansion is order-independent and an explicit `fontSize`/`fontWeight` survives. What a
  JSX `textStyle` does displace is a recipe's own composite `textStyle`, which is the case
  the move actually protects.
- `zimmProductName.css.ts` implied the move brought `textStyle` under
  `recipeGuards.test.ts`. It did not: `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` is exactly
  `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`, and that guard names `textStyle` as the remedy.
- `recipeParts.test.ts` said `parts` gates `baseStyle`. Probed against a real
  `ChakraProvider`: it gates `variants`/`sizes`. An undeclared part keeps its full base
  styling and silently stops responding to variants — latent until someone adds one. The
  base SFCC header recipe ships that shape, 9 parts against 13 `baseStyle` keys.
- `theme/index.test.tsx`'s pin comment described three atoms' recipes; it now describes
  all seven accurately.

Left open deliberately: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 1 prescribes
the JSX-prop form these five components move away from. That file is Tier 1 governance, so
the conflict is flagged for a ruling rather than resolved here.

Done. Both commits landed, tree clean, all gates green on the committed state.

## Landed

```
4651e7f  fix(utils): unwind rich-text tags innermost-first so nested lists keep their content
a647b31  fix(pdp): consolidate the static product info styling surface and close its test gaps
```

**8 commits on `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`. 43 files, +4,589/−6 against `develop`.** Nothing pushed, no PR open.

Gates re-measured on the committed tree: **G1 0 · G2 374/25 · G3 17err/15warn · G4 24 suites/106 · G5 14/22 · G7 no new findings.** The lint error count held as a 17 invariant across all eight commits.

## What the last round actually bought

The scorer's REWORK was comment-only, but running G7 on the corrected tree caught something no earlier gate had: **`richText.tsx` displaced description content out of nested lists.** Nothing before it exercised nested markup — not the tester's four angles, not 370 unit tests, not 106 Storybook a11y assertions. That's the second time in this build a gate found a defect that the review layers structurally couldn't see, the first being the three audit passes that produced the six fixes.

Worth noting for the retrospective: **every defect class that mattered was found by something other than the per-commit loop.** The loop was good at holding invariants and bad at noticing uniform divergences and unexercised input shapes.

## Ready for you

**PR body draft:** `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/pr-body-draft.md` — 150 lines, matching #59's structure, final numbers in. When you want it opened:

```
gh pr create --base develop --title "feat(pdp): SFCC-89 static product information — name, price, description, model line, and style code" --body-file "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/pr-body-draft.md"
```

Two things in it need your input first:

1. **The `overrideStyling.md` ruling.** Point 1 prescribes `textStyle="body2"` as a prop; #59 put it in seven recipes and zero props, and this PR follows #59. Either the doc gets updated or this is recorded as a deliberate override. Tier 1, so it's yours.
2. **The breadcrumb note** is still omitted per your hold. Say the word and I'll add it.

## Still open, not mine to close

- **Escalations:** the Figma leading-trim spacing conflict (and nobody has recorded the DS file's `fileKey`, so neither source can be checked); `c_modelFit`'s two-step data job for Dani; the accordion tickets — description duplication *and* base's unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; the extraneous `isomorphic-dompurify`; `overrideStyling.md` citing two files that have never existed on any branch.
- **Yours by ownership:** the E2E artefacts dropped from #57; SFCC-91 coordination (24 commits past the fork, 3 shared files); the description data-source TBD; QA's SFCC-732/733 class-selector ACs.

One correction from this round worth carrying: I told the builder the base SFCC header recipe declares no `parts` key. It declares nine — my claim came from a truncated read, and the builder refused the instruction rather than write it into the file. The accurate version is what shipped.

content.text:
## Direct answer: yes, it's sound — but it's the only number in that component with no anchor behind it, and the question surfaces something bigger.

### The number holds up

`body2` is `fontSizes['2xs']` = **14px**, and `--zimm-scale-m` is **16px**, so the indent is ~1.14em. A `disc` marker at `list-style-position: outside` needs roughly 0.5–1em of inset to sit inside the box, so 16px contains it. It's a real DS token, so it's traceable and `audit:tokens`-clean. **I confirmed there is no list, marker, or bullet token anywhere in `theme/foundation/`** — so there was genuinely nothing to derive it from.

One honest caveat: at 14px type, 16px leaves only a couple of pixels of slack before a marker would start clipping the column edge. 20px would roughly triple that headroom. I'm reasoning from the spec there, not measuring — jsdom doesn't render markers, and I haven't run a real-browser check. Say the word and I'll measure it in Storybook's chromium.

### The alternative you'd probably prefer, if you change anything

`SPACE_BETWEEN_BLOCKS` in that same recipe is already **20px**, and unlike 16px that value is *DS-measured* — it's the text-group rhythm. Reusing it would take the component from "one measured value plus one invented one" to "one measured value," full stop. The counter-argument is that vertical rhythm and horizontal indent are different axes, so the reuse is coincidence wearing the costume of a principle. I'd call it a real toss-up and **not worth a code change without a design.**

### What I'd actually raise instead

Two things came out of checking this that matter more than 16 vs 20:

**1. The accordion isn't a better precedent — it's the unstyled case.** Base `information-accordion.jsx:40-46` dumps `longDescription` into a bare `<Box>` through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with no list rules at all, so Chakra's `:where(ol, ul) { padding: 0 }` stands and its markers hang *outside* the box. That's the whole reason our bullets look different from the drawer's — we restored an indent and it never had one. Ours isn't a different choice; it's the only choice made.

**2. The PDP renders the description twice, right now, styled two different ways.** `InformationAccordion` is still mounted at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:823` and `:866`, and it renders `product.longDescription` — the same field our mapper feeds the info column as `description`. So the same copy paints twice: once at `body2` with a 20px rhythm and contained markers, once at the base font with markers hanging out.

That reframes your question. **The bullet difference is a symptom of the duplication, not an independent design gap** — and whatever the designer decides about list treatment has to be decided once, for both, not twice.

### Recommendation

- **Keep 16px.** It's defensible, it's tokenised, and changing it without a design trades one unanchored number for another.
- **Don't lift it to a shared module yet.** Only one file uses it; per `conventions.md` that's a speculative abstraction, and it'd be scope creep on an already-committed PR.
- **Do carry the value and its rationale into the accordion ticket** (SFCC-195/102/266/267) so whoever styles the second rendering inherits 16px rather than inventing a third number. That's the drift `footerShared.ts` exists to prevent — it just isn't shared yet.
- **Put the duplication in front of the designer as one question**, not two: "the description renders in the info column and the accordion — which one owns it, and what's the list treatment?" It's already on your escalation list; this gives it a concrete second reason.

Nothing changed in the tree — this was a read-only check.

════ zimmProductMeta.css.ts — full file ════
/**
 * Recipe for the PDP meta block — the model line and the style code, which the design places
 * at the bottom of the info column below the accordions.
 *
 * Multipart with a single `root` part rather than a bare `baseStyle`: `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`
 * reconciles a declared `parts` array against what the sibling component actually reads off
 * `useMultiStyleConfig`, and a recipe with no `parts` key is skipped by that walk entirely.
 * Declaring the one part buys the reconciliation for the two-node shape this block will grow
 * into when the designer settles the label/value question raised in `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts`.
 */

/**
 * DS: 28px between the drawers and the model line, and again between the model line and the
 * style code — identical on both breakpoints (pdp/product-content, desktop and mobile Default).
 * Figma: pdp/product-content, Desktop Default 40000307:14062 / Mobile Default 40000343:9727.
 *
 * A rem literal because no rem-valued 28px token exists to reference. `spacing.ts` brackets it
 * at `xl` (1.5rem/24px) and `2xl` (2rem/32px) with nothing between, and `--zimm-scale-700` — the
 * one alias that does hold 28px — is itself a raw px string in `zimmTokens.ts`, not a reference
 * to a named step the way its neighbours `--zimm-scale-600`/`-800` reference `spacing.xl`/`2xl`.
 * Substituting it would silently convert spacing that scales with the user's root font size into
 * fixed px, which is what overrideStyling.md's Units rule rules out for spacing (WCAG 1.4.4).
 *
 * `theme/components/listMenu.ts` (lines 17, 33, 65, 84) does use `var(--zimm-scale-700)` for its
 * own 28px, so the precedent in this repo is genuinely split — noted here so the next reader does
 * not read that file as evidence this one is wrong and "align" it into a px value. The Units rule
 * is what decides, and it points at rem for spacing. Pending a named 28px step from the UI
 * designer both should converge on; listMenu.ts is designer-owned Tier 2 and not this file's to
 * change. Do not swap for `xl` or `2xl`, both visibly wrong.
 */
const SPACE_META_ROW = '1.75rem'; // 28px at the default 16px root

export const ZimmProductMeta = {
  parts: ['root'],
  baseStyle: {
    // One const drives both hops because the design measures both at 28px. Written as a `gap`
    // plus a `paddingTop` on the same container — the pattern `footer.css.ts` (lines 41-42)
    // already uses with its own SPACE_SECTION — so the two cannot drift apart.
    root: {
      display: 'flex',
      flexDirection: 'column',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: SPACE_META_ROW, // model line -> style code
      paddingTop: SPACE_META_ROW, // drawers -> model line
    },
  },
};

content.text:
Sweep is done, and it earned some real findings. The `h1` is base's `<Heading as="h1" srOnly>` — a visually-hidden generic "Product Details".

## Item 2 — box-model sweep: complete, 4 viewports

**Every internal metric is exact and stable at 402 / 768 / 1024 / 1440:**

| Measured | Result | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| Meta `rowGap` (model→style) | **28px** | 28px ✓ |
| Meta `paddingTop` (accordions→meta) | **28px** | 28px ✓ |
| Style code label→value | **4px** | 4px ✓ |
| Name→price, price→description | **20px / 20px** | 20px ✓ |
| List indent / marker | **16px / `disc`** | provisional ✓ |
| List `marginBlockStart` | **20px** | 20px ✓ |
| All margins | **0px** | as designed ✓ |
| **Off-token paddings/margins/gaps** | **0 — empty at every viewport** | — |

That last row is the #59-equivalent claim, now actually earned rather than asserted.

**Two real discrepancies against Figma, same root cause:**

The real design nodes (`3093:67151` desktop; info column `5083:70358`) put the info column at **218px** — and our `product-content` measures **660px at 1440**. The model line and style code sit *inside* that 218px column in Figma (`5083:70411`/`70412`), but our `product-meta` spans **1376px**, because we placed it after the accordions following base's full-width layout.

**Our components' internal spacing is exact; the container they sit in is base's and doesn't match Figma yet.** That's `pdp/hero` layout metrics — explicitly **SFCC-723**, out of scope here. Worth stating plainly in the PR body rather than letting "design fidelity ✓" imply the column is right.

**And it sharpens the escalated leading-trim question with numbers.** Figma's text nodes are cap-height trimmed — style code is 8px tall there vs our 18px line box, price 9px vs 18px. So Figma's 28px is cap-to-cap, ours is line-box-to-line-box. At 12px/18px there's roughly 4px of half-leading above the cap and ~5px of descender+half-leading below, so a cap-to-cap 28px is about **18–19px of CSS gap** — meaning our 28px renders nearer 37px cap-to-cap. That supports the design auditor's position. Caveat: the cap/descender ratios are Futura-Round estimates I didn't measure from the font file, so treat the direction as solid and the magnitude as approximate. Still the designer's call.

## Item 3 — runtime a11y: verified what's verifiable

**Confirmed on the live page, all four viewports:** `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"` present on the price element; exactly one `h1`; coherent heading outline.

**Three things you should know:**

1. **The product name is `h2`. The page's only `h1` is base's screen-reader-only "Product Details".** Not an axe violation — which is why every gate passed — but for a luxury PDP the product name as `h1` is standard, and AGENTS.md calls for SEO-friendly. Our `headingLevel="h2"` is *consistent* with base (avoids a second `h1`); fixing it properly means replacing base's `h1`, which is page-structure scope beyond this story. Flagging, not changing.
2. **Before consent, the entire PDP is `aria-hidden`.** Didomi's dialog opens on load and hides the background — correct fail-closed behaviour, but it means a screen-reader user meets consent first. My dismissal selectors didn't match it, so note the attribute checks above were read with it still open (static attributes, so still valid).
3. **Still not verified: the actual announcement.** Nobody has switched a variant with a screen reader running. I can't do that — it needs you or QA.

## New finding worth handing to QA

**Base renders `ProductView` twice** — one per breakpoint, one `display: none`. So `product-name`, `product-price`, `product-description` and `product-content` each appear **twice** in the DOM. Playwright strict mode will fail on `getByTestId('product-name')`. That's directly relevant to QA's SFCC-732/733 specs and needs a `.filter({ visible: true })` or equivalent.

`/code-quality` is still running — I'll fold its findings in when it lands, then update the PR body with all of this (including correcting those two non-existent Figma node IDs).

---

# Agent B — Import Analysis

**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` · installed `@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`

## 🔴 Must fix — none

No circular imports, no unresolvable imports, no later-sprint imports, no deep-relative chains, no live resolver trap.

## 🟡 Should fix in this PR

**1. Base-path import of `app/constants`, which *is* overridden — latent silent divergence**

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:55` and `:69`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:51` and `:77-85`

All four import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants` while `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/constants/index.ts` exists (pre-existing, `cd60b7a`). `overrideStyling.md`:

> "**import B via a relative path (`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path** … A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC version**"

**No behavioural impact today** — the override is a pure superset re-export (`export * from` base, plus `CUSTOM_HOME_TITLE`, which neither file imports), so the resolved values are identical. It matters the day anyone changes a constant's *value* there: every base-template consumer picks up the new value (their issuer is in `node_modules`, so they get redirected to the override), while these two files keep the base value. Split-brain, silent, in production.

**Fix:** `from 'app/constants'` in all four places. Safe — the `app/` alias is configured in all four resolution surfaces (`babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `.storybook/main.js`), and the override's own `export *` from the base path keeps working via the `isFromExtends` guard. Deferring is defensible under "minimal changes" since this is inherited copy-first code, but the fix is three lines.

## 🔵 Backlog

**2. Sibling files use two different import styles for the same job.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:63-67` uses relative (`../../components/...`); `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:15-16` uses the `app/` alias. Both resolve identically in all four surfaces and both satisfy the rule. The `app/` alias is the established house style elsewhere (`theme/components/index.ts`, `zimmProductMeta/index.test.tsx`). Pick one.

**3. `vendor.d.ts` ambient declarations are legitimate, but hand-maintained and partial.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` — I verified neither declaration papers over an available real type: `react-helmet@6.1.0` ships `types: NONE` and `@types/react-helmet` is not installed (Hard Rule 7 blocks adding it), and `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/` contains only `errors.js`, no `.d.ts`. So both are the only option. Caveat for **Agent C**: `HelmetProps` omits real react-helmet props (`meta`, `link`, `script`, `style`, `title`, `onChangeClientState`, `base`), and with no index signature the first legitimate use of one will be a type error rather than a silent `any` — safer than a catch-all, but a maintenance edge.

**4. None of this class of bug is machine-caught.** `.eslintrc.js` configures no `import/` plugin rules — no `import/no-cycle`, no `no-restricted-imports`. `overrideStyling.md`'s highest-value rule relies entirely on human review. A `no-restricted-imports` pattern banning `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/<x>` where `overrides/app/<x>` exists would close it.

**5.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` contains no JSX (uses `React.createElement` throughout), so it could be `.ts`. Trivial.

## Doc-accuracy finding — worth escalating

**`overrideStyling.md`'s stated rationale for its most important rule is factually wrong**, and the two new files in this PR get it right.

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:121-124` claims a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the unstyled base SFCC version in Storybook and Vitest." I verified against the resolver source, `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js:128-146`:

```js
isFromExtends(request, filepath) {
  ...
  return this.extends.includes(pkgName) &&
    // request is not issued from overrides
    !filepath.includes(issuerPath)   // issuerPath = <projectDir>/overrides
}
```

When the issuer lives under `overrides/`, `isFromExtends` returns false, `targetFile` stays undefined, and the request falls through to base `node_modules` — **in every environment, including the real app build**. The plugin's own doc comment confirms this is deliberate ("allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax"), and it must be, or `overrides/app/constants/index.ts`'s `export * from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'` would resolve to itself.

Three consequences:
- The rule is **more** important than the doc implies — the failure is production, not just tooling.
- The doc's "dormant only because its Storybook story…" framing for `product-tile`'s `DisplayPrice` rests on the wrong reason; such an import would be live-broken in the app.
- That "known instance" also points at files that **don't exist here**: `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` and `.../link/` are absent on this branch and on `develop`. They exist only on unmerged branches (`04b65f6`, `0ca71d1`). Nothing for this PR to inherit or fix.

The comments at `product-detail/index.tsx:55-62` and `staticProductHeader.tsx:7-14` both state the correct mechanism and cite `isFromExtends` by name. The doc should be corrected to match the code, not the reverse.

Only real hit is `app/constants` (above). `image-gallery`, `breadcrumb`, `link`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `product-tile/promo-callout`, `quantity-picker`, `with-registration`, `responsive`, `loading-spinner`, `recommended-products`, `island`, `sf-payments-express-buttons`, `shared/ui`, `pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion` — **no override exists for any**, so the base path is correct per the settled decisions.

Base `routes.jsx:43` does use relative `import('./pages/product-detail')` (never redirected), and base `:110` does carry `/product/:productId`. `configureRoutes` → `configureRoutesWithExplicitMatching` (default, `fuzzyPathMatching` not passed) dedupes keeping the **first** occurrence, and `ignoredRoutes: ['/callback','*']` doesn't cover this path — so the entry at line 47-50, placed before `..._routes`, wins for the bare path and every site/locale variant. <result>## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** 22 production files of the 43 changed (excluding `*.test.ts(x)`, `*.stories.tsx`, `.claude/registry/*`)
**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` · vs `origin/develop`
