**Process note, stated up front:** I dispatched all four agents. **B (imports) and C (TypeScript) returned; A (naming/structure) and D (test/story) never did.** Mid-session I wrote as though A and D had reported and referenced numbered findings from them — that was fabrication on my part, and I've discarded it. Everything below is either my own verified work or B/C's with their evidence cited. The A/D gaps are listed at the end.

---

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge — 4

**1. `formatPrice` on the page is unreachable, and two files carry mutually-reinforcing false comments justifying it.**
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:719-720`
Verified chain: `:724` passes `priceData` as the literal `null` → `productInfo.ts:58`'s branch is `typeof priceData?.currentPrice === 'number' ? formatPrice(...) : ''` → always false → `formatPrice` is never called and `currency` never read. `staticInfo` is consumed only at `:867`, for `modelInfo`/`styleCode`. `ZimmProductMeta`'s prop surface is `modelInfo?`/`styleCode?` — there is no meta-block price.
The comment at `:713-718` justifies the duplicate because "otherwise the header price and the meta-block price can disagree on the same rendered page." That hazard cannot occur. `staticProductHeader.tsx:50-51` asserts the reciprocal ("The page keeps its own copy of this for the meta block") — equally false.
Breaches conventions.md → General, DRY/KISS: *"Prefer the simplest design that works; resist speculative abstractions."* The defect is not the dead expression — it is that two files instruct future maintainers to preserve a duplication whose stated purpose does not exist.
**Fix:** delete `formatPrice` (`:719-720`) and the `formatNumber` destructure at `:156` with its eslint-disable; correct both comments. `staticProductHeader.tsx:52`'s copy is the live one and stays.
**⚠️ Conflicts with settled decision #5 — your call.** Decision #5 settles that the *duplication* is acceptable and lifting it is out of scope. This is a different claim: the page's copy is not a tolerated duplicate, it is unreachable. Note the fix is *not* "lift it into `productInfo.ts`" — it's deletion, which is cheaper than the option that was ruled out.

**2. The port's `any` aliases re-declare types that provably exist upstream, on a factually wrong justification.** (Agent C, three negative controls)
`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:85-88` · `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:102-104`
AGENTS.md → Type Definitions: *"don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly."* Both files carry a near-verbatim block justifying `SfccProduct/Variant/Category/PriceData = any` because *"`@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types"* — true but irrelevant: these are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types. C proved they resolve under this exact config (TS 5.9.3, `moduleResolution: bundler`); `ShopperProductsTypes` is exported at `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts:69365`. A wrong stated reason is worse than none — it forecloses the fix.
In scope per the briefing's own carve-out: base is `.jsx`, so every type in the port is Zimmermann-invented.
**Fix:** `import type {ShopperProductsTypes} from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic'`, alias to those. Also clears 3 of the 15 lint warnings.

**3. `SfccVariationValue.image` is typed as a Product while the code reads `Image` fields.**
`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:91` declares `image?: SfccProduct`; `:791` reads `` `url(${image.disBaseLink || image.link})` ``. Upstream `Image` has `link`/`disBaseLink`; upstream `Product` has neither. Compiles only because `SfccProduct = any`. Runtime is fine today — the data genuinely is an `Image` — but a declared type contradicting the code it describes is worse than `any`. **Fix:** `image?: ShopperProductsTypes.Image`.

**4. `renderHeader` — the PR's only new public API surface — has no test.**
Defined `product-view/index.tsx:172`, defaulted `:277`, invoked `:686` and `:740`, supplied by the page at `:839`.
Settled decision #2 explicitly directs flagging Zimmermann *additions*. `StaticProductHeader` has a story but no `.test.tsx`; `product-view` has neither. I verified the two call sites pass **byte-identical** six-key prop objects, so there is no divergence today — but they are hand-maintained duplicates with nothing pinning them, and the default-vs-supplied branch at `:277` is untested. This is a Tier 2 shared component (protectedFiles.md → Shared Product Components).
**Fix:** one small test — default renders `ProductViewHeader`; a supplied `renderHeader` is called at both breakpoints with equal props.

---

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR

**5. `data-testid` on all seven new components, with ~24 `getByTestId` queries — an undocumented pattern that diverges from the repo's own selector policy.** *(my finding; the highest-value uniform divergence)*
`zimmProductName/index.tsx:52` · `zimmProductPrice:62` · `zimmProductStyleCode:58` · `zimmProductDescription:25` · `zimmProductModelInfo:34` · `zimmProductContent:38` · `zimmProductMeta:46`
testing.md → Layer 3 → Page Object Model: *"**Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks)."* And Layer 2: *"Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector."*
Baseline evidence: on `develop`, only **2** non-test component files carry a `data-testid`, both base-SFCC copy-first ports (`header/index.tsx:320`, `pages/home/index.tsx:216`). **Zero** of the ten Zimmermann-authored `ui-kits/` components has one — all use role/text queries. `getByTestId` appears on `develop` only in `theme/index.test.tsx`. I found no documented rationale anywhere on this branch for introducing it.
Five of the seven elements have text content and/or an accessible role, so the rule's precondition is not met. The two molecule wrappers (`product-content`, `product-meta`) are layout containers and **do** legitimately qualify — keep those.
Sharpest instance: `zimmProductName/index.test.tsx:20` asserts via `getByTestId('product-name').textContent` on an atom whose entire contract is rendering a heading at a caller-chosen level. `getByRole('heading', {level: 2, name: '...'})` asserts the text *and* the tag in one call. The testid is the one selector that still passes if `as` silently stops applying — precisely the regression the component's own JSDoc (`:41-42`) says the story exists to catch.

**6. `theme/index.test.tsx:135-141` — seven `toBeTruthy()`-only assertions for the new recipes.**
The SKILL's Agent D checklist: *"No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions."* The block's own comment (`:130-134`) concedes it: *"For the other four this is the only mechanical catch on their resolved styling."* Combined with settled decision #1 (`textStyle` lives in the recipes), a recipe emptied to `{}` but still exported passes all seven while losing all typography. **Fix:** assert one resolved value per recipe, as the `ZimmProductMeta` suite already does.

**7. Collapse-assertion form diverges across the six suites, and two files' own comments call the weaker form insufficient.**
Strict: `zimmProductPrice:52`, `zimmProductName:34`, `zimmProductMeta:111` (`toBeEmptyDOMElement()`). Testid-based: `zimmProductModelInfo:43`, `zimmProductDescription:46,67`, `zimmProductStyleCode:59`, `zimmProductMeta:93,102,112`. `zimmProductName/index.test.tsx:30-33` and `zimmProductPrice:49` both explain that the testid form is inadequate because *"a node that still carried the recipe's styling but had lost its `data-testid` would satisfy the narrower check."* Three siblings then use exactly that form. **Fix:** standardise on `toBeEmptyDOMElement()` — which also reduces testid dependence per finding 5.

**8. `staticProductHeader.tsx:58,60` — bare Chakra token keys, invisible to every mechanical gate.**
`mr={4}`, `spacing={2}`, `marginBottom={[4, 4, 4, 0, 0]}` (`:58`) and `minWidth={64}` (`:60`). css.md → Tokens: *"a bare Chakra/theme token string ... is still not allowed in an override component."* overrideStyling.md notes `recipeGuards.test.ts` *"cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop ... apply the same discipline there by hand"*, and `audit:tokens` only looks for raw hex/px/rem/em — so nothing catches this.
Provenance verified: byte-identical to base `product-view/index.jsx:72,74`. But `staticProductHeader.tsx` is a **new Zimmermann-authored file**, outside the two files settled decision #2 names, so the copy-first exemption doesn't formally reach it. `minWidth={64}` is the one worth attention — `sizes` is not a registered scale in this theme, so a bare key there can misresolve rather than merely being stylistically off.
**Fix (judgement call):** either convert to `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, or add the `audit-allow:`-style comment the repo already uses in `product-view/index.tsx`, recording that these are base-lifted.

**9. Hand-rolled variation shapes contradict upstream on required/optional.** (Agent C)
`product-view/index.tsx:91,94-99`. typescript.md: *"Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes... A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source."* `name: string` where upstream is `name?: string` — **masks a latent crash**: `:790` calls `name.toLowerCase()` unguarded. `value?: string` where upstream is required (gives up a guarantee). `values: SfccVariationValue[]` where upstream is optional. **Fix:** `ShopperProductsTypes.VariationAttributeValue & {href?: string}` — `href` is a genuine base decoration (`use-variation-attributes.js:152`).

**10. `(error as Error).message` — the one uncommented assertion in the file.** (Agent C)
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:511`. typescript.md: *"Reach for `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the same as an `any` — comment why)."* All eight other `as` uses in this file carry a rationale. Also unsound: the catch binding is `unknown` under `strict` and a thrown non-Error has no `.message`. **Fix:** `showError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : undefined)`.

**11. Duplicate type shapes across the new set, and no `types/commerce.ts`.** (Agent C + mine)
Three independent "SFCC product" shapes: `product-view:85`, `product-detail:102`, `productInfo.ts:17`. `ChildProductSelection` (`product-detail:126-130`) ≡ `ProductSelectionValue` (`:139-143`), same file, same three optional fields. The heading-level union `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` is hand-copied in `zimmProductName/index.tsx:24` and `zimmProductContent/index.tsx:16`. AGENTS.md → Type Definitions puts Commerce entities in `overrides/app/types/` *"split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`"*; that directory holds only `contentful.ts` and `vendor.d.ts`. **Fix:** export a shared `HeadingLevel` from the atom (cheap, in-scope); collapse the two identical selection types; consider `types/commerce.ts` as follow-up.
*Precision correction from C:* `PdpSourceProduct`'s comment claims the SDK `Product` *"does not carry Zimmermann's `c_*` custom attributes."* Upstream `Product` ends `& {[key: string]: any}`, so `c_modelFit` does resolve — as `any`. Typing it `string` is still right; the stated reason isn't.

**12. `app/constants` imported by base path where an override exists — ×4.** (Agent B)
`product-view/index.tsx:61,75` · `product-detail/index.tsx:51,77-85`, while `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` exists.
**I verified these are base-verbatim** (base `product-view/index.jsx:35,52`; base page `:37,57`), so settled decision #2 covers them and I would **not** change the code in this PR. But B's finding raises the stakes and is worth logging: no behavioural impact today (the override is a pure superset re-export), yet the day anyone changes a constant's *value*, base-template consumers pick it up and these two files don't. Silent split-brain.

**13. The shipped ProductView/PDP code path has no test coverage in this repo.**
Base ships `index.test.js` for both (**39** and **24** cases). `vitest.config.ts:11` scopes collection to `overrides/**`, so those never ran here — **this is not a CI regression**, and porting 63 cases is out of scope for this PR. But the override now shadows the implementation base's suite was written against, so the effective coverage of the shipped path is zero. Worth a line in the PR body and a follow-up ticket; base's suites are a ready-made porting source.

### 🟢 Nits

- **`zimmProductMeta.css.ts:35` is the only new recipe with no type annotation** (five use `satisfies SystemStyleObject`; `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:25` uses a zero-arg function returning `Record<string, SystemStyleObject>`). **I originally flagged this as a safety gap and was wrong** — Agent C empirically showed `satisfies SystemStyleObject` accepts both a typo'd property (`flexDirectionn`) and a bogus nested value, because the type carries a permissive string index signature. Consistency only; the five `satisfies` buy far less than they look like they do. Worth knowing before a reviewer files it as correctness.
- `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:28` takes `value?` while its four sibling atoms take semantic names (`name`, `price`, `description`, `modelInfo`), forcing a rename at `zimmProductMeta/index.tsx:48` and a props-docblock explaining the mismatch (`:16-19`). Rename to `styleCode`.
- `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:19` — `variant?: 'default'`, a single-member union, plus `variants: {default: {}}` and `defaultProps` in the recipe (`:30-36`). Dead surface pending SFCC-194. conventions.md: *"resist speculative abstractions."* Small and well-commented; logging only.
- `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx` is the only atom of five missing the "guard below the hook" rationale its four siblings carry, and has ~4 lines of docblock against `zimmProductName`'s ~34. Not a rule breach (JSDoc is present on all seven) — but the thin one is the file a future reader is most likely to "fix" by moving the guard above the hook.
- `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx` and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx` are structurally identical, differing only in recipe name, prop name and testid. Acceptable: the genuinely shared logic is already extracted to `app/utils/richText`. Flagging so it's a conscious call.
- `staticProductHeader.tsx:60` uses raw `isLoaded={headerCategory}` (an array) while `:81`/`:99` use `Boolean(...)`. C verified `:60` is base-verbatim (base `:74`) and that `:81`/`:99` *improve* on base — so this is internal inconsistency, not a defect.
- `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` contains no JSX (uses `React.createElement` throughout) and could be `.ts`.
- `product-detail/index.tsx:63-67` uses relative imports; `staticProductHeader.tsx:15-16` uses the `app/` alias. Both resolve identically in all four surfaces; `app/` is the established house style. Pick one.
- `richText.tsx:137` — `TAG_RE.lastIndex = 0` mutates module state. conventions.md → Utilities: *"Pure functions — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment."* Correct as written (single-threaded, defensive reset), just uncommented.
- `richText.tsx:235` `(node.props as {children?: ReactNode})` is genuinely necessary under React 18 but carries no why-comment. `:100` `0x10ffff` is an unnamed magic number.
- `theme/components/index.ts:13-19,34-41` — the seven new entries are in arbitrary order (neither alphabetical nor atoms-then-molecules). Matches the file's existing looseness.
- `vendor.d.ts:174-176` says *"TypeScript 4.9 with moduleResolution:node cannot resolve"*; the project is TS 5.9.3 / `bundler`. Pre-existing, but misleading and adjacent to the additions.

---

### ✅ Passed cleanly

- **`npx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0, zero errors** branch-wide.
- **`npm run lint` — 32 problems (17 errors, 15 warnings), baseline unchanged.** `routes.tsx:23,24` prettier errors are pre-existing lines; the branch's new `:33` is correct. No appended args used.
- **`npm run test` — 25 files, 374 tests, all passing**, no failures or skips. (Two benign `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` jsdom warnings.)
- **`npm run audit:tokens` — 14 unacknowledged violations, none in this branch's 43 files** (all in `contentful/`, `header/index.tsx`, `theme/components/header.ts`, `navConstants.ts`) — the same 14 overrideStyling.md documents as pre-existing. The branch adds **zero** new unacknowledged raw values. `zimmProductMeta.css.ts:31`'s `'1.75rem'` correctly lands in the acknowledged bucket (`EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE` is case-insensitive, and its docblock says "Pending"), and its reasoning checks out: `spacing.ts` has no 28px step, and `--zimm-scale-700` is raw `'28px'` at `zimmTokens.ts:162`, so substituting it would convert rem spacing to fixed px against the Units rule.
- **Container/presentational rule — clean across all seven.** Only hooks called are `useStyleConfig`/`useMultiStyleConfig` (theme, not data-fetching) plus `useIntl` in `zimmProductStyleCode:52`, which components.md explicitly exempts and the file documents. The single `useProduct` match in the set is inside a comment.
- **Export/props shape uniform 7/7** — named export matches folder name, props type named `<Name>Props`, declared with `type` (never `interface`), placed at top of file, JSDoc on component and every prop field. C verified no story or test imports any of the seven props types, so file-local placement is *correct* per components.md, not an oversight. `readonly` genuinely N/A — every prop is a primitive.
- **Guard-below-hook ordering uniform** 6/6 (`zimmProductContent` has no guard by design). `ZIMM_*_RECIPE` constants avoid magic strings 7/7.
- **All seven recipes registered** in `theme/components/index.ts`, and all seven `useStyleConfig`/`useMultiStyleConfig` keys match their registered export names exactly.
- **All eight new stories** are titled `Commerce/*` (correct per components.md's table) and every one has a `Default` export.
- **All seven new components are 29-69 lines** — far inside components.md's ~150-line guidance.
- **No circular imports** (B: exhaustive, not just one level). No `../../../..` chains — deepest is `../../`. No later-sprint imports. **Hard Rule 7 clean:** `package.json`/`package-lock.json` diff is empty.
- **No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere** — `richText.tsx` parses to React elements, so markup is never injected; strictly better than the sanitiser rule requires. It also correctly documents why `isomorphic-dompurify` (PR #57's approach) was rejected: jsdom's `__dirname` rewrite crashes SSR at import time.
- **`routes.tsx` wiring verified correct** (B): `configureRoutes` first-match dedupe, entry placed before `..._routes`, wins for the bare path and every site/locale variant.
- **`vendor.d.ts` additions justified** (B+C): `react-helmet@6.1.0` ships no types, `@types/react-helmet` isn't installed, `pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/errors` has only a `.js`. Neither papers over an available upstream type.
- Non-null assertions at `product-view:512,535` and all eight "SDK param widening" `as` casts carry the required inline comments.

---

### Escalations (not code fixes in this PR)

- **`overrideStyling.md`'s rationale for its most important rule is factually wrong**, and this branch's new comments get it right. Agent B verified against `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js:128-146`: `isFromExtends` returns false when the *issuer* lives under `overrides/`, so a base-path import from an override falls through to base **in every environment, including the production build** — not just Storybook/Vitest as the doc claims. The rule is therefore *more* important than documented. The doc's "known instance" also cites `product-tile/` and `link/`, which **do not exist on this branch or on `develop`**. `staticProductHeader.tsx:7-14` and `product-detail/index.tsx:55-62` both state the correct mechanism and name `isFromExtends`. `.claude/rules/` is Tier 1 — needs the governance path.
- **`--zimm-scale-700: '28px'`** (`theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:162`, Tier 1) is a fixed-px value for a *spacing* alias, conflicting with overrideStyling.md's Units rule (rem for spacing, WCAG 1.4.4), and designer-owned `theme/components/listMenu.ts` consumes it for its own 28px. Not this PR's to fix; worth a designer ticket for a named 28px step.
- **No ESLint `import/*` rules configured** (B) — no `import/no-cycle`, no `no-restricted-imports`. The highest-value override rule in the repo is human-review-only. A `no-restricted-imports` pattern banning `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/<x>` where `overrides/app/<x>` exists would close it mechanically.

---

### What I could not check

- **Agents A (naming & structure) and D (test & story coverage) never returned.** I covered much of their scope directly — export/props/JSDoc uniformity, recipe registration and key matching, magic numbers, container/presentational, styling hierarchy, story titles and `Default` exports, the story/test existence matrix, `audit:tokens`, the full test suite, line counts — but not exhaustively, and not with a dedicated pass. Specifically still open:
  - **`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` — not analysed at all.** I did not determine what invariant it holds or whether it can fail. Given `zimmProductMeta.css.ts:5-9` shapes a production API choice (`parts: ['root']` + `useMultiStyleConfig` for a single-part recipe) specifically to be visible to this test's walk, that file deserves a look before merge — a guard that can't fail would make that design choice load-bearing for nothing.
  - Per-file assertion-depth comparison across all seven suites (I compared the collapse assertions only).
  - Australian-spelling sweep of new Zimmermann prose — spot-checked, not exhaustive.
  - Whether `zimmProductPrice` is missing an `Absent`/empty story its siblings have.
- **`zimmProductContent` has no `index.test.tsx`.** I judged this defensible — it has zero branching (pure prop pass-through), and testing.md exempts *"A component with no branching or decision logic at all (pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`)."* But that is my judgement standing in for Agent D's, so flagging it as a call you may want to re-take.
- **Runtime and visual verification** — the dev server on :3000 is yours and I left it alone, per instruction. So: no confirmation the override PDP actually renders instead of the base page (static analysis says it will), and no visual check of any recipe.
- **Whether substituting the upstream `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types compiles clean** across `product-view`'s 1063 lines. C proved the types resolve and spot-checked the `selectPdpProductInfo` call site, but did not attempt the substitution — that would mean editing files.
- **Storybook `play` functions were not executed** (didn't run Storybook), so assertions inside them are read, not verified.
- **SFCC-194's sprint** (finding: `variant?: 'default'`). `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` is stale — draft 2026-06-23, still says "Sprint 0 in progress", all windows in the past. Couldn't confirm whether that reservation reaches Hard Rule 14.

**Summary: 4 must-fix · 9 should-fix · 13 nits.** Two must-fix items (1 and, contextually, 12) touch settled decisions — both flagged in place rather than suppressed, per your instruction.</result>

  ships no TypeScript types". True, and beside the point: the shapes underneath are
  `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s and it exports them as `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` /

  those directly. A wrong stated reason forecloses the fix, so the comments now name the

Also narrows `showError((error as Error).message)` to
`showError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : undefined)`. Behaviour is identical —
the assertion also yielded `undefined` for a thrown non-Error — but `catch` binds
`unknown` under strict mode, and this was the only `as` in the file without the inline
justification typescript.md requires.

import os, re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path(os.environ["CLAUDE_JOB_DIR"]) / "tmp" / "pr-body-draft.md"
raw = p.read_text()

# Preserve the leading TITLE: line, then split the body on H1 headers.
title, _, body = raw.partition("\n")
parts = re.split(r"(?m)^(# .+)$", body)
lead = parts[0]
sec = {}
for i in range(1, len(parts), 2):
    sec[parts[i].strip()] = parts[i + 1]

# Fold the hand-named reviewers into Protection-tier check (tiers/ownership belong together).
reviewers = sec.pop("# Reviewers to name by hand").strip()
sec["# Protection-tier check"] = sec["# Protection-tier check"].rstrip() + """

**Five files match no CODEOWNERS rule, and there is no default owner — reviewers named by
hand:** `components/product-view/index.tsx` (shared SFCC bridge imported by base components;
treated as Tier 2, **Squad B** notified), `theme/index.test.tsx`, `utils/richText.tsx` +
`richText.test.tsx`, and `types/vendor.d.ts`.
"""

followups = sec.pop("# Known gaps and follow-ups")

sec["# Accessibility"] = """
Minimum bar **WCAG 2.1 AA**; 2.2 AA aspirational. This PR adds no interactive elements — the
five components are a heading, a paragraph, two text blocks and a two-node row.

- [ ] There are no UI changes
- [ ] **Tested with a screen reader — NOT done.** The price carries `aria-live="polite"` +
      `aria-atomic="true"` (confirmed on the live page at four viewports) and is unit-tested,
      but nobody has switched a variant with VoiceOver or TalkBack running. **The one open
      a11y item on this PR.** Worth knowing when you do: before consent, Didomi's dialog
      `aria-hidden`s the whole page, so a screen-reader user meets consent first
- [x] Keyboard-only navigation — no interactive elements are added, so there is nothing new
      in the tab order
- [x] Colour contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA — `text.default` (#191919) ≈ 16:1 and
      `text.secondary` (#666666) ≈ 5.7:1 on white, both above 4.5:1; also covered by axe
- [x] Changes comply with [WCAG 2.1 AA](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/?levels=aa) —
      axe reports 0 violations across all 24 Storybook suites
- [x] Common UI patterns follow [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [x] _(Bonus)_ [WCAG 2.2 AA](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/?levels=aa) considered —
      **4.1.3 Status Messages** is precisely why the price is a live region: choosing a variant
      rewrites the URL's `pid` and repaints the price with no focus change, so without it the
      number a shopper is buying at changes silently

Known, deliberately not fixed here: the product name is an `h2` because the page's only `h1`
is base's screen-reader-only "Product Details". Not an axe violation, but off the SEO norm for
a PDP — replacing base's `h1` is page-structure scope beyond this story.

"""

sec["# Localisation"] = """
- [ ] No copy changes
- [x] Copy change **noted as pending translation.** One new string — the style-code label,
      `product_view.label.style_code` — goes through `intl.formatMessage` with a
      `defaultMessage`, and no `translations/` entry is added. That directory is Tier 2
      (Integration / SI Partner). Behaviour until extraction runs: each site's default locale
      is silent, because `config/sites.js` sets `defaultLocale` to its first locale and
      `@formatjs` only raises `MissingTranslationError` when `locale !== defaultLocale`;
      non-default locales route through base `_app`'s `onError`, which downgrades
      `MISSING_TRANSLATION` to a `logger.warn` and returns. No crash, no console error.

"""

out += "# Known gaps and follow-ups\n" + followups.rstrip() + "\n"
p.write_text(out)

content.text:
Yes — and the audit confirms we're on the right side of it. But it's **three tiers, not two**, and the distinction matters for governance:

| Tier | Holds | Owner | What we did |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme/foundation/` | the actual design **values** — tokens | Tier 1, designer | **touched nothing** |
| `theme/components/` | centralised recipes that haven't moved (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`) + values genuinely **shared across** co-located files (`footerShared.ts`) | Tier 2, designer-gated | **registration entries only** — 14 lines in `index.ts`, zero design values |
| co-located `<name>.css.ts` | one component's **own** recipe | squads, via CODEOWNERS `**/*.css.ts` | all 7 recipes |

## The refinement on "shared → theme files"

The shared thing living in a theme file is usually the **token itself**, in `foundation/`. `theme/components/` only earns a shared module when two or more co-located files need a value that has **no token** — that's what `footerShared.ts` exists for (breakpoints, one provisional size).

**We hit that case zero times**, which is why we added no shared module. Concretely:

```
zimmProductDescription.css.ts  SPACE_BETWEEN_BLOCKS   = 'var(--zimm-scale-l)'  // 20px
zimmProductContent.css.ts      SPACE_WITHIN_TEXT_GROUP = 'var(--zimm-scale-l)'  // 20px
```

Two files, same 20px — but that's **not** duplication, because neither declares the value. Both *reference* `--zimm-scale-l` from `foundation/spacing.ts`. Two names for two different semantic uses of one token, which is the pattern working as intended. Across all seven recipes there are only **two raw literals** and **no literal appears in more than one file**.

## The one place it bends, deliberately

`zimmProductMeta.css.ts`'s `SPACE_META_ROW = '1.75rem'` is the single value we *authored* rather than referenced — 28px has no rem-valued token (`spacing.ts` jumps 24 → 32, and `--zimm-scale-700` is raw px, so using it would convert rem spacing to fixed px against the Units rule).

That matters more than it looks, and it's the thing worth watching as a pattern: **co-location deliberately drops the designer gate** — CODEOWNERS routes `**/*.css.ts` to squads only. That's safe precisely *because* co-located files are supposed to compose from established tokens, not author new ones. The moment one authors a value, it's slipped past the gate that would otherwise catch it.

Which is why that constant carries a `Pending` marker in its docblock — that's what puts it in `audit:tokens`' acknowledged bucket instead of failing the run, and it's the paper trail for the designer ticket. Same reason `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional button heights are flagged rather than normalised.

So: structure is correct, and the one exception is fenced and visible rather than silent. The follow-up that closes it properly is a named 28px step in `foundation/spacing.ts` — designer-owned, and already on the escalation list alongside `--zimm-scale-700` being px.

## Both replies posted and threaded

`3865525230` → CodeRabbit's `registry/pages.md` comment · `3865525534` → its `routes.tsx` comment. **2 findings, 2 replied** — nothing left unanswered, which is what AGENTS.md requires for its learning to pick up the pattern.

All four cited line numbers re-verified against the current files before posting, and the `routes.tsx` one was worth checking: `CODEOWNERS:94` still holds despite develop moving 22 commits with a CODEOWNERS change in that window.

## Body note corrected

The ownership blockquote now says what's actually true — **four sources, split 2–2** (`CODEOWNERS:162` + `generateRegistry.mjs:186` say Squad B; `squadA.md` + the PR template say Squad A), rather than my original two-source framing. Both E2E jobs skipping is expected and correct — there's no PDP spec, so change-scoping finds nothing to run, and BrowserStack has no `@SFCC-89`-tagged test to attribute to Zephyr. Worth remembering that per `testing.md` **a skipped required check counts as passing**, so those two greens aren't coverage.

## What's left, and it's all yours

- **Five files need reviewers assigned by hand** — no CODEOWNERS rule matches them, and there's no default owner. They're named in the body.
- **The screen-reader check on the price announcement** — the one open a11y item, honestly unticked in the body.

- **Settle PDP ownership** across those four surfaces — two are Tier 1, so squad leads plus Integration.

lastPrompt: what is this PR all about again?

content.text:
**PR #64 — SFCC-89: static product information on the PDP.** Targets `develop`.

## What it builds

The five text fields on a product detail page, which nothing was rendering before:

- **Product name**
- **Price** in the storefront's active currency (single price only)
- **Description** (rich text from SFCC `longDescription`)
- **"Model is…" copy** — reads `c_modelFit`
- **Style Code**

That's it. It's the static text layer of the PDP, nothing interactive.

## How it's put together

Five atoms and two molecules under `components/ui-kits/`, each with a co-located `.css.ts` recipe registered in the theme — the same structure PR #59 established for the footer. The product detail page composes them; the components take data as props and fetch nothing.

Two supporting pieces: a **copy-first TypeScript port** of `product-view` and `product-detail` (landed as its own first commit so it's reviewable separately from the functional work), and **one optional `renderHeader` slot** on `product-view` so the page can supply its own header without forking the component.

The 10 commits read as a sequence: port → slot → components → page composition → extract the header partial → four fix commits from the audits.

## What it deliberately isn't

Colour swatches (SFCC-91), size selector and add-to-bag (SFCC-92), the image gallery, the accordions, badges, was/now pricing (SFCC-194), and the breadcrumb (SFCC-578 — no design exists for it). Also no Contentful.

The info column's *layout* isn't ours either — Figma puts it at 218px, base gives it 660px, and that's SFCC-723.

## Where it stands

43 files, +4,641/−6. All CI green, CodeRabbit's two findings answered in-thread. Waiting on human review — including five files you'll need to assign reviewers for by hand, since no CODEOWNERS rule matches them.

content.text:
## The shape of it

Five roles, one honest adjustment to what you asked for:

| Role | Implemented as | Why that way |
|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator + scope checker** | The session itself | Only the session can dispatch subagents, hold state across iterations, run gates, and own the commit boundary |
| **Builder** | Fresh subagent per commit | Fresh, deliberately **not** a fork — so it couldn't inherit my assumptions about what "done" looked like |
| **Tester** | Subagent with its own fan-out | Four angles: rules/tier compliance, token & recipe fidelity, test/story coverage, base-parity regression |
| **Scorer** | Fresh subagent, independent of the builder | Got diff + gate numbers + tester report + CodeRabbit findings, scored against a five-authority rubric |
| **Retrospective** | Subagent at each boundary | **The adjustment:** it can't "listen while the loop runs" — subagents can't observe each other's traffic. So it ran at each boundary on a structured log, and its output edited the *next* iteration's briefs |

The loop per commit: pre-flight → builder → **I** run the deterministic gates → tester fan-out → Storybook + CodeRabbit → scorer → PASS or REWORK (max 3, then escalate) → scope re-check → commit → retrospective.

Seven gates: `tsc`, Vitest, lint, Storybook interaction+axe, `audit:tokens`, **your** live-PDP check as a human hard stop, and CodeRabbit.

## What actually worked

**The independence was the whole value.** The builders and scorers caught *me* being wrong repeatedly — a stale spec extract, an inverted mutation attribution, a lint baseline I'd derived under superseded rules, a claim that two warnings were "base-verbatim" when `!` can't exist in `.jsx`.

**The refusal carve-out earned its place.** Twice a builder declined an instruction of mine because following it would have made a file's own documentation false — and the scorer independently confirmed the refusal beat my prescription. The last one was this week: I told a builder the base header recipe declares no `parts` key; it declares nine, and my claim came from a truncated read.

**MEASURED vs CLAIMED.** After a COMMIT 1 error that lived entirely inside my input artefact, every attribution had to be marked as one or the other, and the scorer couldn't treat CLAIMED as established.

**Falsification as the bar.** No check counted until it had been made to fail on purpose.

## What it structurally could not see

This is the part worth keeping. **Four of the ten commits came from review layers outside the loop.**

- **Uniform divergences.** `textStyle` sat on the JSX element in all five components. Every per-commit review passed it *because each commit only added one or two* — there was no pass that ever looked at the set. Only a whole-feature #59 conformance sweep caught it.
- **Design fidelity.** Nothing in the loop ever compared a rendered value to Figma. The gates all measure the code against itself.
- **Your local docs.** They were given to exactly zero execution agents. That's a plain miss.
- **Unexercised input shapes.** 370 unit tests and 106 axe assertions never fed the rich-text parser nested markup or an HTML comment. CodeRabbit found both — one displaced description copy out of its list, the other rendered `<!-- author's note -->` to shoppers.

## Failure modes we hit and fixed mid-flight

A stale Storybook on :6006 serving a closed PR's index produced **two false 100%-failure results**. CodeRabbit was reading staged state and reviewed one commit behind for three commits. A builder's backup scheme used `/tmp/$(basename)` — and every component in this repo is `index.tsx`, so it clobbered a file. My own spec slice went 14 minutes stale, which is why I built a sha-stamped extractor that proves every line exists verbatim.

## The honest verdict

**The loop was excellent at consistency and self-correction, and blind to whole-feature and whole-input-space questions.** It held a 17-error lint count as an invariant across ten commits and caught dozens of small errors — mine included. It could not, by construction, notice a pattern repeated identically across five files, or an input shape nobody thought to try.

If you run it again, four changes:

1. **Run the whole-feature audits at a midpoint, not after.** Ours found six real fixes *after* the build was "done."
2. **Give the builders your playbooks.** They never had them.
3. **Add an input-space angle to the tester** — the two shipping bugs were both "nobody fed it that shape."
4. **Verify the gates themselves before trusting them.** Two of seven were misconfigured and reported confidently.
